title.en: Volume 75 Biographies 25: Su Shizhang, Wei Yunqi, Sun Fujia, Zhang Xuansu
title.raw: 卷七十五 列傳第二十五: 蘇世長 韋雲起 孫伏伽 張玄素 Volume 75 Biographies 25: Su Shizhang, Wei Yunqi, Sun Fujia, Zhang Xuansu

sentences.zh: 蘇世長 子良嗣

translations.literal: Su Shichang; his son Liangsi
translations.idiomatic: Su Shichang; his son Liangsi

sentences.zh: 韋雲起 孫方質

translations.literal: Wei Yunqi; his grandson Fangzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunqi; his grandson Fangzhi

sentences.zh: 孫伏伽 張玄素

translations.literal: Sun Fujia; Zhang Xuansu
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fujia; Zhang Xuansu

sentences.zh: 蘇世長，雍州武功人也。

translations.literal: Su Shichang was a man of Wugong in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shichang was a native of Wugong in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖彤，後魏直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tong was Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary in the Secretariat of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong had served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary in the Secretariat under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父振，周宕州刺史、建威縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Governor of Dangzhou under Zhou and Marquis of Jianwei County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had been Governor of Dangzhou under the Northern Zhou and Marquis of Jianwei County.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，世長年十餘歲，上書言事。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, Shichang was a little more than ten years old and submitted a memorial on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou was on the throne, Shichang, still only in his early teens, submitted a memorial on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其年小，召問：「讀何書？

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his youth, summoned him and asked, "What books have you read?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, thinking him very young, summoned him and asked, "What books have you read?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「讀《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: " He replied, "I have read the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I have read the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects."

sentences.zh: 」武帝曰：「《孝經》、《論語》何所言？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "What do the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects say?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "What do those books say?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「《孝經》云：『為國者不敢侮於鰥寡。

translations.literal: " He replied, "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'He who governs a state does not dare to slight widowers and widows.'"
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The Classic of Filial Piety says that one who governs the state must not slight widowers and widows."

sentences.zh: 』《論語》云：『為政以德。

translations.literal: The Analects says, 'To govern is to practice virtue.'"
translations.idiomatic: And the Analects says that to govern is to practice virtue."

sentences.zh: 』」武帝善其對，令於獸門館讀書。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his answer and had him study at the Beast Gate Academy.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased with his answer and ordered him to study at the Beast Gate Academy.

sentences.zh: 以其父歿王事，因令襲爵，世長於武帝前擗踴號泣，武帝為之改容。

translations.literal: Because his father had died in the service of the state, he was ordered to inherit the title; before the Emperor, Shichang beat his breast and stamped his feet, wailing aloud, and the Emperor's expression changed on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in the state's service, he was ordered to inherit the family title; in the emperor's presence Shichang beat his breast and wailed until the emperor's face softened.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，世長又屢上便宜，頗有補益，超遷長安令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Shichang again repeatedly submitted practical proposals, which were quite beneficial, and he was promoted out of turn to Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Shichang again submitted many practical proposals that proved genuinely useful, and he was promoted ahead of schedule to magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為都水少監，使於上江督運。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was Vice Director of the Directorate of Waterways and was sent to the upper Yangtze to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he served as vice director of the Directorate of Waterways and was dispatched to the upper Yangtze to supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 會江都難作，世長為煬帝發喪慟哭，哀感路人。

translations.literal: When the Jiangdu catastrophe occurred, Shichang held mourning for Emperor Yang and wept bitterly, his grief moving passersby.
translations.idiomatic: When the catastrophe at Jiangdu struck, Shichang held mourning rites for Emperor Yang and wept until passersby were moved by his grief.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭號，署為太子太保、行台右僕射。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he appointed him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Right Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, he appointed Shichang Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and right vice director of the mobile secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與世充兄子弘烈及將豆盧褒俱鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Shichong's nephew Honglie and the general Doulu Bao, he garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was stationed at Xiangyang together with Wang Shichong's nephew Honglie and the general Doulu Bao.

sentences.zh: 時弘烈娶褒女為妻，深相結托。

translations.literal: At that time Honglie had married Bao's daughter, and they were deeply bound to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie had by then married Bao's daughter, and the two men were bound to each other in a close alliance.

sentences.zh: 高祖與褒有舊，璽書諭之，不從，頻斬使者。

translations.literal: Gaozu had old ties with Bao and sent imperial letters to instruct him, but he would not obey and repeatedly executed envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had known Bao in earlier days and sent sealed imperial letters urging him to submit, but Bao refused and repeatedly put the envoys to death.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，洛陽平，世長首勸弘烈歸降。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Luoyang was pacified, Shichang was the first to urge Honglie to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, after Luoyang fell, Shichang was the first to urge Honglie to surrender.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，高祖誅褒而責世長來晚之故，世長頓顙曰：「自古帝王受命，為逐鹿之喻，一人得之，萬夫斂手。

translations.literal: When they reached the capital, Gaozu executed Bao and reproached Shichang for coming late; Shichang bowed his forehead to the ground and said, "From antiquity, when emperors received the Mandate, it was likened to chasing deer—when one man got it, ten thousand men withdrew their hands."
translations.idiomatic: After they reached the capital, Gaozu executed Bao and rebuked Shichang for arriving too late. Shichang pressed his forehead to the ground and said, "Since antiquity the receiving of Heaven's mandate has been likened to the hunt for the deer: once one man has seized it, all the others must withdraw their hands."

sentences.zh: 豈有獲鹿之後，忿同獵之徒，問爭肉之罪也？

translations.literal: How could there be, after the deer is taken, anger at fellow hunters and inquiry into the crime of quarreling over the meat?
translations.idiomatic: Surely there is no precedent for, after the deer has been taken, turning in anger on one's fellow hunters and prosecuting them for quarreling over the meat?

sentences.zh: 陛下應天順人，布德施惠，又安得忘管仲、雍齒之事乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has responded to Heaven and followed the people, spreading virtue and bestowing grace—how could you forget the cases of Guan Zhong and Yong Chi!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has answered Heaven and won the people, spreading virtue and bestowing grace—how could you forget what was done for Guan Zhong and Yong Chi?

sentences.zh: 且臣武功之士，經涉亂離，死亡略盡，惟臣殘命，得見聖朝，陛下若復殺之，是絕其類也。

translations.literal: Moreover, I am a man of Wugong; having passed through turmoil and separation, the dead are nearly all gone, and only my remnant life remains to see the sage court—if Your Majesty kills me again, you will cut off our kind.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I am a man of Wugong. Our district has passed through rebellion and ruin until almost none of us are left; only my wretched life remains to see this enlightened age. If Your Majesty kills me now, you will extinguish our whole line.

sentences.zh: 實望天恩，使有遺種。

translations.literal: I truly hope for Heaven's grace that there may be descendants left.
translations.idiomatic: I truly beg for Heaven's grace that some of us may be left to carry on the line.

sentences.zh: 」高祖與之有故，笑而釋之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu had old ties with him, laughed, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu had known him in earlier days, laughed, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 尋授玉山屯監。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Supervisor of the Yushan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed supervisor of the Yushan garrison.

sentences.zh: 後於玄武門引見，語及平生，恩意甚厚。

translations.literal: Later he was received in audience at the Xuanwu Gate; they spoke of their whole lives, and the favor shown was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was received in audience at the Xuanwu Gate; as they spoke of their whole lives together, the emperor showed him exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿自謂諂佞耶，正直耶？

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Do you consider yourself fawning and sycophantic, or upright?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked, "Do you take yourself for a flatterer, or for an upright man?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣實愚直。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your servant is truly dull and upright."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I am simply dull and bluntly honest."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿若直，何為背世充而歸我？

translations.literal: " Gaozu said, "If you are upright, why did you turn against Shichong and come to me?"
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "If you are so upright, why did you abandon Shichong and come over to me?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「洛陽既平，天下為一，臣智窮力屈，始歸陛下。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Once Luoyang was pacified and the realm was one, your servant's wits were exhausted and his strength spent—only then did I come to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Once Luoyang fell and the realm was united, my wits were exhausted and my strength spent—only then did I submit to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 向使世充尚在，臣據漢南，天意雖有所歸，人事足為勍敵。

translations.literal: Had Shichong still been alive and your servant held the south of Han, though Heaven's intent might have had its destination, in human affairs I would have been a formidable foe."
translations.idiomatic: Had Shichong still been alive while I held the south of Han, Heaven's intent might already have had its chosen lord, but in human terms I would still have been a formidable enemy."

sentences.zh: 」高祖大笑。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 嘗嘲之曰：「名長意短，口正心邪，棄忠貞於鄭國，忘信義於吾家。

translations.literal: He once mocked him, saying, "Long in name but short in intent, upright in mouth but crooked in heart—you abandoned loyalty in the state of Zheng and forgot faith toward our house."
translations.idiomatic: He once teased him, saying, "Long in name but short in purpose, upright of speech but crooked of heart—you abandoned loyalty in Zheng and forgot your obligations to our house."

sentences.zh: 」世長對曰：「名長意短，實如聖旨；

translations.literal: " Shichang replied, "Long in name but short in intent—that is indeed as Your Majesty says;"
translations.idiomatic: " Shichang replied, "Long in name but short in purpose—that much is exactly as Your Majesty says;"

sentences.zh: 口正心邪，未敢奉詔。

translations.literal: upright in mouth but crooked in heart—I dare not accept that edict."
translations.idiomatic: but as for upright of speech and crooked of heart, I dare not accept that part of the edict."

sentences.zh: 昔竇融以河西降漢，十世封侯；

translations.literal: In former times Dou Rong surrendered the Hexi region to Han and his line was enfeoffed as marquises for ten generations;"
translations.idiomatic: In former times Dou Rong surrendered the Hexi to Han and his line held marquisates for ten generations;"

sentences.zh: 臣以山南歸國，惟蒙屯監。

translations.literal: your servant came to the state from south of the mountains and has received only a garrison supervisorship."
translations.idiomatic: I came in from south of the mountains and have received only a garrison supervisorship."

sentences.zh: 」即日擢拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: " That same day he was promoted and appointed Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: " That very day he was promoted to remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 從幸涇陽校獵，大獲禽獸於旌門。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor on a hunting expedition at Jingyang and took a great catch of game at the Banner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on a hunting expedition at Jingyang, where a great haul of game was taken at the Banner Gate.

sentences.zh: 高祖入御營，顧謂朝臣曰：「今日畋樂乎？

translations.literal: Gaozu entered the imperial camp, turned to the court officials, and said, "Was today's hunt enjoyable?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu entered the imperial camp, turned to the officials, and asked, "Was today's hunt a pleasure?"

sentences.zh: 」世長進曰：「陛下遊獵，薄廢萬機，不滿十旬，未為大樂。

translations.literal: " Shichang advanced and said, "Your Majesty's hunting slightly neglects the myriad affairs of state; in less than a hundred days it will not count as great pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: " Shichang stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty's hunting already lightly neglects the myriad affairs of state. In less than a hundred days this will hardly count as great pleasure."

sentences.zh: 」高祖色變，既而笑曰：「狂態發耶？

translations.literal: " Gaozu's expression changed; then he laughed and said, "Has your wild streak broken out?"
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu's face darkened; then he laughed and said, "Has your wild streak come out again?"

sentences.zh: 」世長曰：「為臣私計則狂，為陛下國計則忠矣。

translations.literal: " Shichang said, "By your servant's private reckoning it is wild; by reckoning for Your Majesty's state it is loyal."
translations.idiomatic: " Shichang said, "By my private reckoning it is wild; by reckoning for Your Majesty's realm it is loyal."

sentences.zh: 」及突厥入寇，武功郡縣，多失戶口，是後下詔將幸武功校獵。

translations.literal: " When the Turks invaded, Wugong commandery and its counties lost many registered households; afterward an edict was issued that the emperor would visit Wugong for a hunting expedition.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Turks raided, Wugong and its counties lost many registered households; afterward an edict announced that the emperor would visit Wugong for a hunting expedition.

sentences.zh: 世長又諫曰：「突厥初入，大為民害，陛下救恤之道猶未發言，乃於其地又縱畋獵，非但仁育之心有所不足，百姓供頓，將何以堪？

translations.literal: Shichang remonstrated again, saying, "The Turks have just entered and greatly harmed the people; Your Majesty has not yet spoken a word on the way of relief and succor, yet in that very place you again let loose the hunt—not only is the heart of humane nurture insufficient, but how can the people's supplies and provisions bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: Shichang remonstrated again: "The Turks have only just invaded and done great harm to the people, yet Your Majesty has not yet uttered a word about relief—and now in that very region you propose to hunt again. This falls short not only of humane governance but of what the people can possibly supply. How can they bear it?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖不納。

translations.literal: " Gaozu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗引之於披香殿，世長酒酣，奏曰：「此殿隋煬帝所作耶？

translations.literal: He also once had him brought to the Puxiang Hall; when Shichang was drunk, he submitted, "Was this hall built by Emperor Yang of Sui?"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he had him brought to the Puxiang Hall. When Shichang was well into his cups, he said, "Was this hall built by Emperor Yang of Sui?"

sentences.zh: 是何雕麗之若此也？

translations.literal: Why is the carving and splendor like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Why is it carved and adorned to such a degree?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿好諫似真，其心實詐。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said, "You love to remonstrate and seem sincere, but your heart is truly deceitful."
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "You love to remonstrate and seem sincere, but your heart is truly deceitful."

sentences.zh: 豈不知此殿是吾所造，何須設詭疑而言煬帝乎？

translations.literal: Do you not know that this hall was built by me—why must you set up a crafty suspicion and speak of Emperor Yang?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you not know that I built this hall myself? Why must you feign ignorance and speak of Emperor Yang?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣實不知。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your servant truly did not know."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I truly did not know."

sentences.zh: 但見傾宮鹿台琉璃之瓦，並非受命帝王愛民節用之所為也。

translations.literal: I only see tiles of tilted palaces, Deer Terrace, and glazed ware—not what an emperor who has received the Mandate does when he loves the people and practices frugality."
translations.idiomatic: I only see the sort of tilted palaces, Deer Terrace, and glazed tiles that no emperor who has received the Mandate builds when he loves the people and practices frugality."

sentences.zh: 若是陛下作此，誠非所宜。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty made this, it is truly not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty built this, it is truly not fitting."

sentences.zh: 臣昔在武功，幸常陪侍，見陛下宅宇，才蔽風霜，當此之時，亦以為足。

translations.literal: In former days at Wugong I was fortunate often to attend you and saw Your Majesty's residence—barely sheltering from wind and frost; even then I thought it sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: In former days at Wugong I was fortunate enough often to attend you. Your residence then barely kept out wind and frost, yet even then you thought it sufficient."

sentences.zh: 今因隋之侈，民不堪命，數歸有道，而陛下得之，實謂懲其奢淫，不忘儉約。

translations.literal: Now, because of Sui's extravagance, the people could not bear their lot and repeatedly turned to the Way; Your Majesty obtained it—I truly thought you would punish their luxury and debauchery and not forget thrift.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because Sui's extravagance drove the people beyond endurance, the realm repeatedly turned to the righteous way until Your Majesty won it. I truly believed you would punish that luxury and debauchery and never forget thrift.

sentences.zh: 今初有天下，而於隋宮之內，又加雕飾，欲撥其亂，寧可得乎？

translations.literal: You have just gained the realm, yet within the Sui palaces you add carving and ornament—wishing to dispel disorder, can that be achieved?"
translations.idiomatic: You have only just won the realm, yet within the Sui palaces you add carving and ornament. If you wish to dispel disorder, how can that be achieved?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖深然之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 後歷陝州長史、天策府軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chief Administrator of Shanzhou and Libationer for Military Counsel of the Heavenly Stratagem Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as chief administrator of Shanzhou and libationer for military counsel in the Prince of Qin's Heavenly Stratagem Office.

sentences.zh: 秦府初開文學館，引為學士。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin's Literary Academy was first opened, he was brought in as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin first opened his Literary Academy, Shichang was brought in as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 與房玄齡等一十八人皆蒙圖畫，令文學褚亮為之贊，曰：「軍諮諧噱，超然辯悟。

translations.literal: Together with Fang Xuanling and seventeen others, he was all granted painted portraits; the literary scholar Chu Liang was ordered to compose encomia for them, saying, "Military counsel, harmonious and witty, transcendent in debate and insight."
translations.idiomatic: He and Fang Xuanling and seventeen others were all granted painted portraits, and the literary scholar Chu Liang was ordered to compose encomia. Of Shichang he wrote, "Military counsel, harmonious and witty, transcendent in debate and insight."

sentences.zh: 正色於庭，匪躬之故。

translations.literal: Upright in countenance at court—for the sake of not sparing himself."
translations.idiomatic: Upright of countenance in court—for the sake of not sparing himself."

sentences.zh: 」貞觀初，聘於突厥，與頡利爭禮，不受賂遺，朝廷稱之。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Zhenguan he was sent on a mission to the Turks; he disputed precedence with Jieli and would not accept bribes or gifts—the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " Early in Zhenguan he was sent on a mission to the Turks. He disputed precedence with Jieli and refused bribes and gifts, and the court praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 出為巴州刺史，覆舟溺水而卒。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Bazhou, capsized in a boat, drowned, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Bazhou, capsized in a boat, drowned, and died.

sentences.zh: 世長機辯有學，博涉而簡率，嗜酒，無威儀。

translations.literal: Shichang was quick-witted and learned, broadly versed yet plain and direct, fond of wine, and without dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was quick-witted and learned, broadly versed yet plain and unceremonious, fond of wine, and without dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 初在陝州，部內多犯法，世長莫能禁，乃責躬引咎，自撻於都街。

translations.literal: When he was first in Shanzhou, within his jurisdiction many broke the law; Shichang could not stop it, so he blamed himself and accepted guilt, flogging himself in the capital street.
translations.idiomatic: While he was in Shanzhou, crime within his jurisdiction was rampant and he could not suppress it. He took the blame on himself and had himself flogged in the main street of the prefectural capital.

sentences.zh: 伍伯嫉其詭，鞭之見血，世長不勝痛，大呼而走，觀者咸以為笑，議者方稱其詐。

translations.literal: The ward headmen, resenting his trickery, flogged him until blood showed; Shichang could not bear the pain, cried out loudly, and ran off—onlookers all thought it laughable, and commentators then called it deceit.
translations.idiomatic: The ward headmen, resenting what they took for a trick, flogged him until the blood showed. Shichang could not bear the pain, cried out, and fled. The onlookers all laughed, and commentators pronounced it a sham.

sentences.zh: 子良嗣，高宗時遷周王府司馬。

translations.literal: His son Liangsi, in Gaozong's time, was transferred to be Chief Administrator of the Prince of Zhou's household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liangsi, under Emperor Gaozong, was appointed chief administrator of the Prince of Zhou's household.

sentences.zh: 王時年少，舉事不法，良嗣正色匡諫，甚見敬憚。

translations.literal: The prince was then young and did many unlawful things; Liangsi with stern countenance corrected and remonstrated, and was greatly respected and feared.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was still young and often acted unlawfully. Liangsi remonstrated with stern countenance and was greatly respected and feared.

sentences.zh: 王府官屬多非其人，良嗣守文檢括，莫敢有犯，深為高宗所稱。

translations.literal: Many of the prince's household officials were not the right men; Liangsi upheld the regulations and inspected them, and none dared offend—Gaozong deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the prince's household officials were unworthy men. Liangsi enforced the regulations strictly, and none dared transgress. Emperor Gaozong praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 遷荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Chief Administrator of the Jingzhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief administrator of the Jingzhou metropolitan area command.

sentences.zh: 高宗使宦者緣江采異竹，將於苑中植之。

translations.literal: Gaozong sent eunuchs along the river to gather exotic bamboo to plant in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong sent eunuchs along the Yangtze to gather exotic bamboo for planting in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 宦者科舟載竹，所在縱暴。

translations.literal: The eunuchs requisitioned boats to carry the bamboo and everywhere let loose violence.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs requisitioned boats to carry the bamboo and committed outrages wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 還過荊州，良嗣囚之，因上疏切諫，稱：「遠方求珍異以疲道路，非聖人抑己愛人之道。

translations.literal: On their return they passed through Jingzhou; Liangsi imprisoned them and submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance, saying, "Seeking rare things from afar and exhausting the roads is not the way of the sage who restrains himself and loves others."
translations.idiomatic: On their return they passed through Jingzhou. Liangsi imprisoned them and submitted a stern memorial, saying, "To seek rare things from afar and exhaust the roads is not the way of a sage who restrains himself and loves others."

sentences.zh: 又小人竊弄威福，以虧皇明。

translations.literal: Moreover, petty men usurp authority and favor, to the detriment of imperial brilliance."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, petty men usurp authority and favor, to the detriment of Your Majesty's brilliance."

sentences.zh: 」言甚切直。

translations.literal: " His words were very stern and direct.
translations.idiomatic: " His language was very stern and direct.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，高宗下制慰勉，遽令棄竹於江中。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Gaozong issued an edict of consolation and encouragement and immediately ordered the bamboo thrown into the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, Emperor Gaozong issued an edict of consolation and encouragement and immediately ordered the bamboo thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，為雍州長史。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era he was Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun era he served as chief administrator of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時關中大飢，人相食，盜賊縱橫。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong suffered great famine; people ate one another and bandits ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guanzhong suffered a terrible famine. People ate one another, and bandits were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 良嗣為政嚴明，盜發三日內無不擒扌適。

translations.literal: Liangsi's governance was strict and clear; within three days of any theft, none went uncaptured.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi governed with strict clarity: no theft reported within three days went uncaptured.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zetian held court, he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu held court, he was promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 尋代王德真為納言，累封溫國公。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he replaced Wang Dezhen as Chief Minister and was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Wenguo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Wang Dezhen as chief minister and was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Wenguo.

sentences.zh: 為西京留守，則天賦詩餞送，賞遇甚渥。

translations.literal: He was made Protector-General of the Western Capital; Zetian composed a poem to send him off, and the favor shown was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed protector-general of the Western Capital. Empress Wu composed a farewell poem for him, and the honors shown him were very generous.

sentences.zh: 時尚方監裴匪躬檢校西苑，將鬻苑中果菜以收其利。

translations.literal: At that time the Director of the Palace Workshops Pei Feigong was inspecting the Western Park and intended to sell the park's fruits and vegetables for profit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Feigong, director of the Palace Workshops, was inspecting the Western Park and intended to sell its fruits and vegetables for profit.

sentences.zh: 良嗣駁之曰：「昔公儀相魯，猶能拔葵去織，未聞萬乘之主，鬻其果菜以與下人爭利也。

translations.literal: Liangsi refuted him, saying, "In former times when Gongyi was chancellor of Lu, he could still uproot melons and remove weaving—one has never heard of a lord of ten thousand chariots selling his fruits and vegetables to compete for profit with his inferiors."
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi objected: "In former times, when Gongyi served as chancellor of Lu, he uprooted his melons and removed his weaving looms. One has never heard of a sovereign of ten thousand chariots selling palace fruits and vegetables to compete for profit with his subjects."

sentences.zh: 」匪躬遂止。

translations.literal: " Feigong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Feigong then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 無幾，追入都，遷文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to the capital and transferred to Left Chancellor of the Wenchang Office, with the same third rank as the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital and promoted to left chancellor of the Wenchang Office with third rank equal to the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace.

sentences.zh: 載初元年春，罷文昌左相，加位特進，仍依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Zai Chu he was removed as Left Chancellor of the Wenchang Office, given the special advancement rank, and still continued to manage state affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Zai Chu he was removed as left chancellor of the Wenchang Office, granted the special advancement rank, and still continued to manage state affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 與地官尚書韋方質不協，及方質坐事當誅，辭引良嗣，則天特保明之。

translations.literal: He was not on good terms with Wei Fangzhi, Minister of the Department of State Affairs; when Fangzhi was implicated in a crime and was to be executed, his testimony implicated Liangsi, but Zetian specially protected and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was on bad terms with Wei Fangzhi, minister of the Department of State Affairs. When Fangzhi was implicated in a capital crime, his testimony implicated Liangsi, but Empress Wu specially protected and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 良嗣謝恩拜伏，便不能復起，輿歸其家，詔御醫張文仲、韋慈藏往視疾。

translations.literal: Liangsi thanked the grace and bowed prostrate but could not rise again; he was carried home in a litter, and an edict ordered the imperial physicians Zhang Wenchong and Wei Cizang to go view his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi thanked her for the grace and bowed prostrate, but could not rise again. He was carried home in a litter, and an edict ordered the imperial physicians Zhang Wenchong and Wei Cizang to attend him.

sentences.zh: 其日薨，年八十五。

translations.literal: That day he died; he was eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same day, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 則天輟朝三日，舉哀於觀風門，敕百官就宅赴吊。

translations.literal: Zetian suspended court for three days, held mourning at the Gate for Viewing the Wind, and ordered the hundred officials to go to his residence to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu suspended court for three days, held mourning at the Gate for Viewing the Wind, and ordered all officials to go to his residence to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，益州都督，賜絹布八百段、米粟八百碩，兼降璽書弔祭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Master with the Glory of the Palace and Area Commander of Yizhou, granted eight hundred bolts of silk cloth and eight hundred piculs of grain, and an imperial letter of condolence was also sent down.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand master with the glory of the palace and area commander of Yizhou, granted eight hundred bolts of silk and eight hundred piculs of grain, and an imperial letter of condolence was also sent down.

sentences.zh: 其子踐言，太常丞，尋為酷吏所陷，配流嶺南而死。

translations.literal: His son Jianyan was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; shortly afterward he was framed by a cruel official, banished to Lingnan, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianyan was vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Before long he was framed by a cruel official, banished to Lingnan, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 追削良嗣官爵，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Liangsi's offices and titles were posthumously stripped and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi's offices and titles were posthumously stripped and his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 景龍元年，追贈良嗣司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinglong, Liangsi was posthumously given the office of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinglong, Liangsi was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 踐言子務玄，襲爵溫國公，開元中，為邠王府長史。

translations.literal: Jianyan's son Wuxuan inherited the title Duke of Wenguo; in the Kaiyuan era he was Chief Administrator of the Prince of Bin's household.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyan's son Wuxuan inherited the title Duke of Wenguo. During the Kaiyuan era he served as chief administrator of the Prince of Bin's household.

sentences.zh: 韋雲起，雍州萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Yunqi was a man of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunqi was a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯父澄，武德初國子祭酒、綿州刺史。

translations.literal: His uncle Cheng was Director of the Imperial University and Governor of Mianzhou at the beginning of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Cheng had served as director of the Imperial University and governor of Mianzhou at the beginning of Wude.

sentences.zh: 雲起，隋開皇中明經舉，授符璽直長。

translations.literal: Yunqi passed the Mingjing examination in the Kaihuang era of Sui and was appointed Director of Seals in the Regular Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi passed the Mingjing examination under Sui in the Kaihuang era and was appointed director of seals in the regular office.

sentences.zh: 嘗因奏事，文帝問曰：「外間有不便事，汝可言之。

translations.literal: Once when presenting business, Emperor Wen asked, "If there are inconvenient matters outside, you may speak of them."
translations.idiomatic: Once when presenting business at court, Emperor Wen asked him, "If anything outside is amiss, you may speak of it."

sentences.zh: 」時兵部侍郎柳述在帝側，雲起應聲奏曰：「柳述驕豪，未嘗經事，兵機要重，非其所堪，徒以公主之婿，遂居要職。

translations.literal: " At that time Vice Minister of War Liu Shu was at the emperor's side. Yunqi responded at once, submitting, "Liu Shu is arrogant and overbearing, has never managed affairs, and military affairs are weighty—he is not fit for them. He holds an important post only because he is the princess's son-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Vice Minister of War Liu Shu stood at the emperor's side. Yunqi answered at once: "Liu Shu is arrogant and overbearing and has never managed affairs. Military affairs are weighty and beyond his capacity. He holds an important post only because he is the princess's son-in-law."

sentences.zh: 臣恐物議以陛下官不擇賢，濫以天秩加於私愛，斯亦不便之大者。

translations.literal: Your servant fears public opinion will hold that Your Majesty does not select the worthy for office but recklessly adds Heaven's rank to private affection—that too is a great inconvenience."
translations.idiomatic: I fear public opinion will say that Your Majesty does not choose the worthy for office but recklessly bestows Heaven's rank out of private affection. That too is a grave inconvenience."

sentences.zh: 」帝甚然其言，顧謂述曰：「雲起之言，汝藥石也，可師友之。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly approved his words and turned to Liu Shu, saying, "Yunqi's words are medicine and whetstone for you—you may take him as teacher and friend."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor strongly approved and turned to Liu Shu. "Yunqi's words are medicine and whetstone for you. You should take him as teacher and friend."

sentences.zh: 」仁壽初，詔在朝文武舉人，述乃舉雲起，進授通事舍人。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Renshou an edict ordered civil and military officials at court to recommend men; Shu then recommended Yunqi, who was promoted to Palace Envoy for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: " At the beginning of Renshou an edict ordered officials at court to recommend talent. Shu recommended Yunqi, who was promoted to palace envoy for diplomatic reception.

sentences.zh: 大業初，改為通事謁者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was changed to Visitor for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye he was redesignated visitor for diplomatic reception.

sentences.zh: 又上疏奏曰：「今朝廷之內多山東人，而自作門戶，更相剡薦，附下罔上，共為朋黨。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial saying, "Today within the court there are many men from east of the mountains, and they form their own factions, slandering and recommending one another, flattering those below and deceiving those above, together forming cliques."
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial: "Today the court is full of men from east of the mountains who form their own factions, slandering and recommending one another, flattering subordinates and deceiving superiors, and banding together in cliques."

sentences.zh: 不抑其端，必傾朝政，臣所以痛心扼腕，不能默已。

translations.literal: If this is not checked at the root, court governance will surely be overturned—this is why your servant is heart-stricken and wrings his wrists and cannot keep silent."
translations.idiomatic: If this is not checked at the root, the government will surely be overturned. That is why I am heart-stricken and cannot keep silent."

sentences.zh: 謹件朋黨人姓名及奸狀如左。

translations.literal: I respectfully list the names of clique members and their wicked conduct as follows."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully list the names of clique members and their misconduct below."

sentences.zh: 」煬帝令大理推究，於是左丞郎蔚之、司隸別駕郎楚之並坐朋黨，配流漫頭赤水，余免官者九人。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yang ordered the Court of Judicial Review to investigate; thus Left Assistant Minister Lang Weizhi and Censorate Assistant Lang Chuzhi were both punished as clique members, banished to Mantou Chishui, and nine others were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Yang ordered the Court of Judicial Review to investigate. Left Assistant Minister Lang Weizhi and Censorate Assistant Lang Chuzhi were both convicted as clique members and banished to Mantou Chishui; nine others were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入抄營州，詔雲起護突厥兵往討契丹部落。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided Yingzhou, an edict ordered Yunqi to lead Turkic troops to attack the Khitan tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided Yingzhou, an edict ordered Yunqi to lead Turkic troops against the Khitan tribes.

sentences.zh: 啟民可汗發騎二萬，受其處分。

translations.literal: Qaghan Qimin dispatched twenty thousand horsemen subject to his disposal.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Qimin dispatched twenty thousand horsemen under his command.

sentences.zh: 雲起分為二十營，四道俱引，營相去各一里，不得交雜。

translations.literal: Yunqi divided them into twenty camps, advancing by four routes together, camps each a li apart, not to intermingle.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi divided them into twenty camps advancing along four routes, each camp a li apart and forbidden to intermingle.

sentences.zh: 聞鼓聲而行，聞角聲而止，自非公使，勿得走馬。

translations.literal: On hearing drum, march; on hearing horn, halt; unless on public business, do not gallop horses.
translations.idiomatic: At the drum they marched; at the horn they halted. Unless on official business, no one might gallop.

sentences.zh: 三令五申之後，擊鼓而發，軍中有犯約者，斬紇幹一人，持首以徇。

translations.literal: After three commands and five instructions, drums sounded and they set out; when someone in the army violated the rules, one Qaghan man was beheaded and the head displayed.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated orders, the drums sounded and the army set out. When a man violated the rules, one Turk was beheaded and his head displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥將帥來入謁之，皆膝行股戰，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Turkic generals came in to pay respects; all crawled on their knees trembling and dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Turkic commanders came to pay their respects, crawling on their knees and trembling, not daring to look up.

sentences.zh: 契丹本事突厥，情無猜忌，雲起既入其界，使突厥詐雲，向柳城郡欲共高麗交易，勿言營中有隋使，敢漏洩者斬之。

translations.literal: The Khitan had formerly served the Turks and were without suspicion. After Yunqi entered their territory, he had the Turks feign that they were going toward Liucheng commandery to trade with Goguryeo, and not speak of a Sui envoy in the camp—whoever leaked would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had long served the Turks and were without suspicion. Once Yunqi entered their territory, he had the Turks pretend they were heading to Liucheng commandery to trade with Goguryeo and forbid any mention of a Sui envoy in camp—leakers would be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 契丹不備。

translations.literal: The Khitan were unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were caught unprepared.

sentences.zh: 去賊營百里，詐引南度，夜復退還，去營五十里，結陣而宿，契丹弗之知也。

translations.literal: A hundred li from the enemy camp they feigned marching south, then at night returned; fifty li from the camp they formed battle lines and encamped—the Khitan did not know.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li from the enemy camp they feigned marching south, then returned by night. Fifty li from the camp they formed ranks and encamped, and the Khitan knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 既明，俱發，馳騎襲之，盡獲其男女四萬口，女子及畜產以半賜突厥，余將入朝，男子皆殺之。

translations.literal: When day dawned all set out, galloping cavalry raided them, capturing entirely forty thousand men and women; women and livestock half were given to the Turks, the rest taken to court, and the men were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they all set out. Galloping cavalry struck and captured forty thousand men and women in all. Women and livestock were half given to the Turks; the rest were sent to court, and the men were all killed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝大喜，集百官曰：「雲起用突厥而平契丹，行師奇譎，才兼文武，又立朝謇諤，朕今親自舉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was greatly pleased and assembled officials, saying, "Yunqi used the Turks to pacify the Khitan—his campaigning was strange and devious, his talent both civil and military; he also stands at court with blunt remonstrance. I now personally promote him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was delighted and assembled the officials. "Yunqi used the Turks to pacify the Khitan," he said. "His campaigning was cunning, his talent both civil and military, and at court he speaks bluntly. I now promote him myself."

sentences.zh: 」擢為治書御史。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 雲起乃奏劾曰：「內史侍郎虞世基，職典樞要，寄任隆重；

translations.literal: Yunqi then submitted impeachment, saying, "Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji holds the pivot of power, his commission weighty and grave;"
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi then submitted an impeachment: "Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji holds the pivot of power and bears a weighty commission;"

sentences.zh: 御史大夫裴蘊，特蒙殊寵，維持內外。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun especially received extraordinary favor and sustained inner and outer affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun has received extraordinary favor and controls affairs within and without the court."

sentences.zh: 今四方告變，不為奏聞，賊數實多，或減言少。

translations.literal: Now alarms come from the four directions but they do not report them; the bandits are really numerous but they reduce the numbers when they speak.
translations.idiomatic: Alarms now come from every quarter, yet they do not report them. The rebels are in fact numerous, yet they understate the numbers.

sentences.zh: 陛下既聞賊少，發兵不多，眾寡懸殊，往皆莫克，故使官軍失利，賊黨日滋。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, having heard the bandits are few, sends not many troops; crowd and few hang far apart, in the past none could overcome, so government troops lose and bandits daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Because Your Majesty hears that the rebels are few, you send few troops. When many and few are so mismatched, defeat has always followed, government armies lose, and the rebels grow daily.

sentences.zh: 此而不繩，為害將大，請付有司，詰正其罪。

translations.literal: If this is not punished, the harm will be great. I request handing them to the responsible office to investigate and correct their crimes."
translations.idiomatic: If this is not punished, the harm will be great. I ask that they be handed to the responsible offices to answer for their crimes."

sentences.zh: 」大理卿鄭善果奏曰：「雲起詆訾名臣，所言不實，非毀朝政，妄作威權。

translations.literal: " Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo submitted, "Yunqi slanders famous ministers; what he says is untrue; he does not slander court governance but presumptuously wields authority."
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo submitted, "Yunqi slanders eminent ministers. His charges are false. He does not criticize the government but presumptuously wields authority."

sentences.zh: 」由是左遷大理司直。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was demoted to Judicial Review Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he was demoted to judicial review assessor.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸揚州，雲起告歸長安，屬義旗入關，於長樂宮謁見。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang visited Yangzhou, Yunqi asked leave to return to Chang'an; when the righteous banner entered the pass, he had audience at the Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang went to Yangzhou, Yunqi asked leave to return to Chang'an. When the righteous banner entered the pass, he had audience at the Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 義寧元年，授司農卿，封陽城縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yining he was appointed Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed Duke of Yangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yining he was appointed minister of agriculture and enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，加授上開府儀同三司，判農圃監事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was additionally given Superlative Grand Master with the Glory of the Palace and directed agricultural and park affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was additionally granted superlative grand master with the glory of the palace and put in charge of agricultural and park affairs.

sentences.zh: 是歲，欲大發兵討王世充，雲起上表諫曰：「國家承喪亂之後，百姓流離，未蒙安養，頻年不熟，關內阻飢。

translations.literal: That year, when they intended to launch a great army to attack Wang Shichong, Yunqi submitted a table remonstrating, saying, "Since the state has endured turmoil, the people are displaced and have not received repose and nurture; years in succession have not ripened; within the passes famine blocks the way."
translations.idiomatic: That year, when a great army was to be raised against Wang Shichong, Yunqi submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Since the state has endured turmoil, the people are displaced and unreconciled; harvests have failed year after year, and famine grips the interior."

sentences.zh: 京邑初平，物情未附，鼠竊狗盜，猶為國憂。

translations.literal: The capital has just been pacified and popular sentiment has not yet attached; rats stealing and dogs banditing still worry the state.
translations.idiomatic: The capital has only just been pacified and popular sentiment has not yet settled. Petty theft and banditry still trouble the state.

sentences.zh: 盩厔司竹，余氛未殄；

translations.literal: Zhazhou and Sizhu, remaining vapors not yet extinguished;"
translations.idiomatic: At Zhazhou and Sizhu, lingering unrest has not yet been extinguished;"

sentences.zh: 藍田、谷口，群盜實多。

translations.literal: Lantian and Gukou, bandits in fact many.
translations.idiomatic: at Lantian and Gukou bandits are in fact numerous.

sentences.zh: 朝夕伺間，極為國害。

translations.literal: Morning and evening they watch for openings—extremely harmful to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening they watch for openings and are extremely harmful to the state.

sentences.zh: 雖京城之內，每夜賊發。

translations.literal: Even within the capital, every night bandits strike.
translations.idiomatic: Even within the capital, bandits strike every night.

sentences.zh: 北有師都，連結胡寇，斯乃國家腹心之疾也。

translations.literal: In the north is Shidu, joining Hu bandits—this is a disease of the state's heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: In the north is Shidu, allied with barbarian raiders—this is a disease at the state's very heart.

sentences.zh: 舍此不圖，而窺兵函、洛，若師出之後，內盜乘虛，一旦有變，禍將不小。

translations.literal: Abandoning consideration of this to look with troops toward Han and Luo—if after the army goes out internal bandits seize the void, once there is change, disaster will not be small.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon concern for this and cast troops toward Han and Luo—if after the army marches out internal bandits seize the opening, once trouble arises the disaster will not be small.

sentences.zh: 臣謂王世充遠隔千里，山川懸絕，無能為害，待有餘力，方可討之。

translations.literal: Your servant considers Wang Shichong far separated by a thousand li, mountains and rivers suspended and cut off, unable to do harm; wait until there is surplus strength, then one may attack him.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Wang Shichong is a thousand li away, cut off by mountains and rivers, and unable to do harm. Wait until there is surplus strength, then attack him.

sentences.zh: 今內難未弭，且宜弘於度外。

translations.literal: Now internal troubles are not yet quelled—we should for the time being enlarge tolerance beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Internal troubles are not yet settled; for now you should practice magnanimity beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，請暫戢兵，務穡勸農，安人和眾。

translations.literal: As your servant's foolish view, I request temporarily resting troops, striving at farming and encouraging agriculture, settling the people and harmonizing the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, I ask that you temporarily rest the armies, devote yourself to farming, and settle and harmonize the people.

sentences.zh: 關中小盜，自然寧息。

translations.literal: Small bandits within the passes will naturally be quieted.
translations.idiomatic: Petty bandits within the passes will naturally subside.

sentences.zh: 秦川將卒，賈勇有餘，三年之後，一舉便定。

translations.literal: Generals and soldiers of Qinchuan still have courage in surplus; in three years one strike will settle all.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and soldiers of Qinchuan still have courage to spare. In three years one stroke will settle everything.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲速，臣恐未可。

translations.literal: Now though you wish speed, your servant fears it cannot yet be done.
translations.idiomatic: Though you wish speed now, I fear it cannot yet be done."

sentences.zh: 」乃從之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they followed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 會突厥入寇，詔雲起總領豳、寧已北九州兵馬，便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Turks invaded, an edict ordered Yunqi to command military forces of the nine prefectures north of Bin and Ning and act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded, an edict ordered Yunqi to command the military forces of the nine prefectures north of Bin and Ning and act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 四年，授西麟州刺史，司農卿如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Governor of Xilinzhou, still Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed governor of Xilinzhou while retaining his post as minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 尋代趙郡王孝恭為夔州刺史，轉遂州都督，懷柔夷獠，鹹得眾心。

translations.literal: Shortly he replaced Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong as Governor of Kuizhou, transferred to Area Commander of Suizhou, soothing the Yi and Liao—all won popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong as governor of Kuizhou, then became area commander of Suizhou, where he soothed the Yi and Liao peoples and won all hearts.

sentences.zh: 遷益州行台民部尚書，尋轉行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the People of the Yizhou Mobile Secretariat, then transferred to Minister of War of the mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of the people of the Yizhou mobile secretariat, then to minister of war of the same secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行台僕射竇軌多行殺戮，又妄奏獠反，冀得集兵。

translations.literal: Mobile Secretariat Deputy Director Dou Gui often carried out executions, and falsely memorialized that the Liao rebelled, hoping to gather troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Secretariat Deputy Director Dou Gui often carried out executions and falsely memorialized that the Liao had rebelled, hoping to gather troops.

sentences.zh: 因此作威，肆其凶暴，雲起多執不從。

translations.literal: Thereby he exercised power and indulged violence; Yunqi often held and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he tyrannized and indulged his violence, while Yunqi often resisted and refused to follow.

sentences.zh: 雲起又營私產，交通生獠，以規其利，軌亦對眾言之，由是構隙，情相猜貳。

translations.literal: Yunqi also managed private property and trafficked with uncivilized Liao to seek profit; Gui also said this publicly to the assembly, whereby suspicion was built and feelings mutually doubting.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi also amassed private property and dealt with uncivilized Liao for profit. Gui also said this publicly, and from this suspicion arose and mutual distrust grew.

sentences.zh: 隱太子之死也，敕遣軌息馳驛詣益州報軌，軌乃疑雲起弟慶儉、堂弟慶嗣及親族並事東宮，慮其聞狀或將為變，先設備而後告之。

translations.literal: At the hidden crown prince's death, an edict sent Gui's son by fast post to Yizhou to inform Gui; Gui then suspected Yunqi's younger brother Qingjian, cousin Qingsi, and kin all served the eastern palace, fearing that hearing the matter they might create trouble, first made preparations then reported.
translations.idiomatic: At the death of the hidden crown prince, an edict sent Gui's son by fast courier to inform him at Yizhou. Gui suspected Yunqi's younger brother Qingjian, his cousin Qingsi, and other kin who had served the eastern palace, fearing that on hearing the news they might rebel. He made preparations first, then announced the matter.

sentences.zh: 雲起果不信，問曰：「詔書何在？

translations.literal: Yunqi truly did not believe and asked, "Where is the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi did not believe it and asked, "Where is the edict?"

sentences.zh: 」軌曰：「公，建成黨也，今不奉詔，同反明矣。

translations.literal: " Gui said, "Sir, you are a party of Jiancheng; now not obeying the edict, rebellion is clear."
translations.idiomatic: " Gui said, "You are a partisan of Jiancheng. By refusing the edict now, your rebellion is plain."

sentences.zh: 」遂執殺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，雲起年少時，師事太學博士王頗，頗每與之言及時事，甚嘉嘆之，乃謂之曰：「韋生識悟如是，必能自取富貴；

translations.literal: Initially when Yunqi was young he studied under Imperial Academy Doctor Wang Po; Po whenever spoke with him of current affairs greatly admired and sighed, and said to him, "Student Wei understands and comprehends thus—you will surely obtain wealth and honor yourself;"
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yunqi studied under Imperial Academy Doctor Wang Po. Whenever Po spoke with him of current affairs he greatly admired him and said, "Student Wei understands so well—you will surely win wealth and honor for yourself;"

sentences.zh: 然剛腸嫉惡，終當以此害身。

translations.literal: but your stiff bowels hate evil—you will ultimately harm yourself thereby."
translations.idiomatic: but your unyielding hatred of evil will ultimately destroy you."

sentences.zh: 」竟如頗言。

translations.literal: " It ended just as Po said.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end it happened just as Po had said.

sentences.zh: 子師實，垂拱初，官至華州刺史、太子少詹事，封扶陽郡公。

translations.literal: His son Shibao, at the beginning of Chuigong, reached Governor of Huazhou and Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed Duke of Fuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shibao, at the beginning of Chuigong, rose to governor of Huazhou and junior steward of the heir apparent, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Fuyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 師實子方質，則天初鸞台侍郎、地官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Shibao's son Fangzhi, at the beginning of Zetian was Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace, Minister of State Affairs, and Grand Counselor equal to the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Shibao's son Fangzhi, at the beginning of Empress Wu's reign, was vice director of the Phoenix Terrace, minister of state affairs, and grand counselor equal to the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace.

sentences.zh: 時改修《垂拱格式》，方質多所損益，甚為時人所稱。

translations.literal: At that time they were revising the Chuigong statutes and formats; Fangzhi made many additions and deletions and was greatly praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chuigong statutes and formats were being revised, Fangzhi made many additions and deletions and was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 俄而武承嗣、三思當朝用事，諸宰相咸傾附之。

translations.literal: Before long Wu Chengsi and Sansi held power at court; all the chief ministers bent to attach to them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi held power at court, and all the chief ministers bent to attach themselves to them.

sentences.zh: 方質疾假，承嗣等詣宅問疾，方質據床不為之禮。

translations.literal: Fangzhi was on sick leave; Chengsi and others went to his residence to inquire after illness, and Fangzhi lay on the bed and did not pay them courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzhi was on sick leave. Chengsi and the others came to his house to inquire after his health, but Fangzhi lay on his bed and did not rise to receive them.

sentences.zh: 左右云：「踞見權貴，恐招危禍。

translations.literal: Those at his side said, "Sitting crouched to see the powerful—you fear inviting calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him said, "To sit crouched before the powerful—you will invite disaster."

sentences.zh: 」方質曰：「吉凶命也。

translations.literal: " Fangzhi said, "Misfortune and fortune are fate."
translations.idiomatic: " Fangzhi said, "Fortune and misfortune are a matter of fate."

sentences.zh: 大丈夫豈能折節曲事近戚，以求苟免也。

translations.literal: A great man—how can he bend his integrity and flatter close kin to seek escape?"
translations.idiomatic: How can a true man bend his integrity and flatter imperial kin merely to save himself?"

sentences.zh: 」尋為酷吏周興、來子珣所構，配流儋州，仍籍沒其家。

translations.literal: " Before long he was framed by cruel officials Zhou Xing and Lai Zixun, banished to Danzhou, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was framed by the cruel officials Zhou Xing and Lai Zixun, banished to Danzhou, and his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 神龍初雪免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously vindicated.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously vindicated.

sentences.zh: 臣聞天子有諍臣，雖無道不失其天下；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that a son of Heaven has remonstrating ministers—even if without the Way he does not lose his realm under Heaven;"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a son of Heaven has remonstrating ministers—even if he is without the Way, he will not lose the realm under Heaven;"

sentences.zh: 父有諍子，雖無道不陷於不義。

translations.literal: a father has remonstrating sons—even if without the Way he does not fall into unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: a father has remonstrating sons—even if he is without the Way, he will not fall into unrighteousness.

sentences.zh: 故云子不可不諍於父，臣不可不諍於君。

translations.literal: Thus it is said a son may not fail to remonstrate with his father, a minister may not fail to remonstrate with his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said that a son must remonstrate with his father and a minister must remonstrate with his lord.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，臣之事君，猶子之事父故也。

translations.literal: Speaking thus, a minister's serving his lord is like a son's serving his father.
translations.idiomatic: In this sense, a minister's service to his lord is like a son's service to his father.

sentences.zh: 隋後主所以失天下者，何也？

translations.literal: Why then did the late emperor of Sui lose the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Why then did the last emperor of Sui lose the realm?

sentences.zh: 止為不聞其過。

translations.literal: It was only because he did not hear his faults.
translations.idiomatic: It was only because he never heard of his faults.

sentences.zh: 當時非無直言之士，由君不受諫，自謂德盛唐堯，功過夏禹，窮侈極欲，以恣其心。

translations.literal: At that time it was not that there were no straight-speaking men—because the lord did not accept remonstrance, he himself considered his virtue greater than Tang Yao, his merit surpassing Xia Yu, exhausting extravagance to the limit to indulge his heart.
translations.idiomatic: It was not that there were no straight-speaking men in his day. Because the ruler would not accept remonstrance, he considered his virtue greater than Tang Yao and his merit surpassing Yu the Great, and exhausted every extravagance to indulge his desires.

sentences.zh: 天下之士，肝腦塗地，戶口減耗，盜賊日滋，而不覺知者，皆由朝臣不敢告之也。

translations.literal: Men under Heaven had their livers and brains smeared on the ground, registered households decreased, bandits daily increased—and he was unaware—all because court ministers dared not tell him.
translations.idiomatic: Men under Heaven had their lives destroyed, registered households dwindled, and bandits multiplied daily—yet he remained unaware, all because his ministers dared not tell him.

sentences.zh: 向使修嚴父之法，開直言之路，選賢任能，賞罰得中，人人樂業，誰能搖動者乎？

translations.literal: If formerly they had practiced the law of the stern father, opened the road of straight speech, selected the worthy and employed the able, rewards and punishments balanced, every man delighted in his occupation—who could shake them?
translations.idiomatic: Had he practiced the law of the stern father, opened the road of frank speech, chosen the worthy and employed the able, and kept rewards and punishments fair so that every man delighted in his work—who could have shaken him?

sentences.zh: 所以前朝好為變更，不師古訓者，止為天誘其咎，將以開今聖唐也。

translations.literal: Therefore the previous dynasty liked to make changes and did not take ancient instruction as master—it was only Heaven inducing their blame, about to open the present sage Tang.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the previous dynasty loved change and would not follow ancient instruction: Heaven was drawing out their guilt to open the way for the present sage Tang.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍舉晉陽，天下響應，計不旋踵，大位遂隆。

translations.literal: Your Majesty rose as a dragon from Jinyang; the realm responded; plans did not turn on the heel and the great position was soon elevated.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rose like a dragon from Jinyang; the realm answered at once; before you could turn on your heel the great throne was yours.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿以唐得天下之易，不知隋失之不難也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not because Tang gained the realm under Heaven easily not know that Sui's losing it was not hard.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not think that because Tang won the realm easily, Sui lost it with difficulty.

sentences.zh: 陛下貴為天子，富有天下，動則左史書之，言則右史書之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is exalted as son of Heaven, possessing the realm; when you move the left historian records it, when you speak the right historian records it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is exalted as son of Heaven and possesses the realm. When you move, the left historian records it; when you speak, the right historian records it.

sentences.zh: 既為竹帛所拘，何可恣情不慎？

translations.literal: Already bound by bamboo and silk, how can you indulge feeling without care?
translations.idiomatic: Already bound by what will be written on bamboo and silk, how can you indulge your feelings without care?

sentences.zh: 凡有搜狩，須順四時，既代天理，安得非時妄動？

translations.literal: All hunting must accord with the four seasons; having replaced Heaven's reason, how can you act out of season rashly?
translations.idiomatic: All hunting must follow the four seasons. Having taken Heaven's place in governing, how can you act rashly out of season?

sentences.zh: 陛下二十日龍飛，二十一日有獻鷂雛者，此乃前朝之弊風，少年之事務，何忽今日行之！

translations.literal: Your Majesty on the twentieth day flew as a dragon; on the twenty-first there was one who presented a fledgling hawk—this is the corrupt practice of the previous dynasty, the business of youth—why suddenly act it today!
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day Your Majesty ascended the throne; on the twenty-first someone presented a fledgling hawk. This is a corrupt practice of the previous dynasty, a youthful amusement—why revive it today!

sentences.zh: 又聞相國參軍事盧牟子獻琵琶，長安縣丞張安道獻弓箭，頻蒙賞勞。

translations.literal: Also heard that Military Affairs Aide to the Chief Minister Lu Mouzi presented a pipa, Chang'an County Assistant Zhang Andao presented bow and arrows, repeatedly receiving rewards and labor.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that Military Affairs Aide to the Chief Minister Lu Mouzi presented a pipa and Chang'an County Assistant Zhang Andao presented bow and arrows, and both have repeatedly received rewards.

sentences.zh: 但「普天之下，莫非王土；

translations.literal: But "All under Heaven, none is not the king's land;"
translations.idiomatic: But "All under Heaven, none is not the king's land;"

sentences.zh: 率土之濱，莫非王臣」，陛下必有所欲，何求而不得？

translations.literal: "Along the shores of the land, none is not the king's minister"—Your Majesty surely has what you desire, what seeking yet not obtain?
translations.idiomatic: "Along the shores of the land, none is not the king's minister." Whatever Your Majesty desires, what could you not obtain?

sentences.zh: 陛下所少者，豈此物哉！

translations.literal: What Your Majesty lacks—is it these things!
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty lacks—is it these trifles!

sentences.zh: 願陛下察臣愚忠，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to examine your servant's foolish loyalty—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider my foolish loyalty, and the realm will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：

translations.literal: The second says:
translations.idiomatic: The second says:

sentences.zh: 百戲散樂，本非正聲，有隋之末，大見崇用，此謂淫風，不可不改。

translations.literal: Hundred entertainments and scattering music are originally not correct sound; at the end of Sui they were greatly honored—this is called lewd wind and cannot but be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Hundred entertainments and scattering music are not proper music. At the end of Sui they were greatly honored. This is lewd custom and cannot go unchanged.

sentences.zh: 近者，太常官司於人間借婦女裙襦五百餘具，以充散妓之服，雲擬五月五日於玄武門遊戲。

translations.literal: Recently the Court of Imperial Sacrifices borrowed from among the people more than five hundred women's skirts and robes to serve as costume for scattering performers, planning on the fifth day of the fifth month to play at the Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Court of Imperial Sacrifices borrowed more than five hundred women's skirts and robes from the populace for scattering performers' costumes, planning games at the Xuanwu Gate on the fifth day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 臣竊思審，實損皇猷，亦非貽厥子孫謀，為後代法也。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects deeply—this truly damages imperial plan, and is also not planning for posterity nor establishing law for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection I find that this truly harms Your Majesty's grand design. It is neither planning for your descendants nor setting an example for later ages.

sentences.zh: 故《書》云：「無以小怨為無傷而弗去。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says: "Do not take a small grievance as harmless and not remove it."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "Do not treat a small grievance as harmless and fail to remove it."

sentences.zh: 」恐從小至於大故也。

translations.literal: " One fears that from small it comes to great, therefore."
translations.idiomatic: " For fear that what is small may grow into something great."

sentences.zh: 《論語》云：「放鄭聲，遠佞人。

translations.literal: The Analects says: "Ban the music of Zheng; keep sycophants at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: "Ban the music of Zheng and keep sycophants at a distance."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「樂則《韶》舞。

translations.literal: " It also says: "For music, the Shao dance."
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "For music, use the Shao dance."

sentences.zh: 」以此言之，散妓定非功成之樂也。

translations.literal: " Speaking thus, scattering performers are certainly not music of accomplished merit."
translations.idiomatic: " By this reasoning, scattering performers are certainly not the music of a successful reign."

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，請並廢之。

translations.literal: As your servant's foolish view, I request abolishing them all.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, I ask that they all be abolished.

sentences.zh: 則天下不勝幸甚。

translations.literal: Then the realm will not bear how greatly fortunate it is.
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm will be beyond fortunate.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：

translations.literal: The third says:
translations.idiomatic: The third says:

sentences.zh: 臣聞性相近而習相遠，以其所好相染也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that natures are close but practice makes distant, because what they love stains one another.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that human natures are alike at birth but diverge through habit, because people are dyed by what they love.

sentences.zh: 故《書》云：「與治同道罔弗興，與亂同事罔弗亡。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says: "Those who share the Way with order will none fail to rise; those who share deeds with chaos will none fail to perish."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "Those who walk the path of order will all prosper; those who share in deeds of chaos will all perish."

sentences.zh: 」以此言之，興亂其在斯與！

translations.literal: " Speaking thus, whether order rises or chaos—lies here!"
translations.idiomatic: " In this sense, whether order rises or chaos is decided here!"

sentences.zh: 皇太子及諸王等左右群僚，不可不擇而任之也。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the various princes' attendants and group of subordinates cannot but be selected before being entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the various princes' attendants and staff must be carefully chosen before they are entrusted with office.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，但是無義之人，及先來無賴，家門不能邕睦；

translations.literal: As your servant's foolish view, all who are without righteousness, and those who came before as ruffians, whose households cannot be harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, all who are without righteousness, former ruffians, and those whose families cannot live in harmony;

sentences.zh: 及好奢華馳獵馭射，專作慢游狗馬、聲色歌舞之人，不得使親而近之也。

translations.literal: and those who love luxury, racing hunts, driving and archery, who devote themselves to idle roaming, horses and dogs, sound, color, and song-dance—must not be allowed to draw near.
translations.idiomatic: and those who love luxury, hunting, driving, and archery, who devote themselves to idle roaming, horses and dogs, music, women, and dancing—must not be allowed to draw near.

sentences.zh: 此等止可悅耳目，備驅馳，至於拾遺補闕，決不能為也。

translations.literal: Such persons can only please the ear and eye and serve as runners; as for remedying oversights and filling gaps, they certainly cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: Such men can only please the senses and serve as runners; as for remedying oversights and filling gaps in governance, they are utterly useless.

sentences.zh: 臣歷窺往古，下觀近代，至於子孫不孝，兄弟離間，莫不為左右亂之也。

translations.literal: Your servant has surveyed ancient times and looked down at recent ages; as for unfilial sons and discord among brothers, none is not caused by attendants causing disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I have surveyed antiquity and observed recent times: unfilial sons and discord among brothers have invariably been caused by attendants sowing disorder.

sentences.zh: 願陛下妙選賢才，以為皇太子僚友，如此即克隆盤石，永固維城矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would wonderfully select worthy talent to serve as the crown prince's companions—thus you will duplicate bedrock solidity and forever secure the walled city.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to choose worthy talent as companions for the crown prince; thus you will secure the realm as firmly as bedrock and make the imperial house an everlasting bulwark.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽之大悅，下詔曰「秦以不聞其過而亡，典籍豈無先誡？

translations.literal: Gaozu read it and was greatly pleased and issued an edict saying, "Qin perished from not hearing its faults—do the classics not have prior admonitions?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read it with great delight and issued an edict: "Qin perished because it never heard of its faults—do the classics not contain warnings from antiquity?"

sentences.zh: 臣僕諂諛，故弗之覺也。

translations.literal: Ministers and servants flattered and fawned, therefore he did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Its ministers flattered and fawned, and so the ruler never perceived it.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖反正，從諫如流。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han rectified the deviation and followed remonstrance as flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han restored order and followed remonstrance as readily as flowing water.

sentences.zh: 洎乎文、景繼業，宣、元承緒，不由斯道，孰隆景祚？

translations.literal: Down to Wen and Jing continuing the enterprise, Xuan and Yuan inheriting the thread—without this Way, who could elevate the imperial fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Down through Wen and Jing continuing the enterprise, and Xuan and Yuan inheriting the mandate—without this Way, who could have elevated the imperial fortune?

sentences.zh: 周、隋之季，忠臣結舌，一言喪邦，諒足深誡。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou and Sui, loyal ministers sealed their tongues; one word lost the state—surely enough for deep warning.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhou and Sui, loyal ministers sealed their tongues; a single word could lose the state—surely warning enough for deep reflection.

sentences.zh: 永言於此，常深嘆息。

translations.literal: Ever speaking of this, I constantly sigh deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on this, I sigh deeply.

sentences.zh: 朕每惟寡薄，恭膺寶命，雖不能性與天道，庶思勉力，常冀弼諧，以匡不逮。

translations.literal: I every time reflect on my few meager qualities, reverently receiving the precious mandate; though I cannot match nature with the Way of Heaven, I hope to strive with effort and constantly look to harmony in assistance to correct my inadequacies.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly reflect on my few and meager qualities and reverently bear the precious mandate. Though I cannot match my nature to the Way of Heaven, I hope to strive with all my strength and constantly look to worthy assistance to correct my shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 而群公卿士，罕進直言，將申虛受之懷，物所未諭。

translations.literal: Yet the host of ministers and great officers rarely present straight words; I will express the receptivity of empty acceptance—what others have not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my ministers and great officers rarely offer frank counsel. I wish to show my willingness to receive it openly, though others have not understood this.

sentences.zh: 萬年縣法曹孫伏伽，至誠慷慨，詞義懇切，指陳得失，無所迴避。

translations.literal: Wannian County Legal Aide Sun Fujia, utmost sincere and generous, words and meaning earnest, pointing out gains and losses, nowhere evading.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fujia, legal aide of Wannian County, has shown utmost sincerity and generosity. His words are earnest, he points out what is right and wrong, and he evades nothing.

sentences.zh: 非有不次之舉，曷貽利行之益！

translations.literal: Unless there is out-of-order promotion, how can there be benefit of conduct carried to others!
translations.idiomatic: Unless he receives extraordinary promotion, how can others be encouraged to act for the public good!

sentences.zh: 伏伽既懷諒直，宜處憲司，可治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Fujia already harbors honesty and straightness—he should occupy the law office; may appoint Deliberating Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fujia already possesses honesty and forthrightness and should serve in the legal offices. Let him be appointed Deliberating Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仍頒示遠近，知朕意焉。

translations.literal: Still proclaim far and near so they may know my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed far and wide so all may know my intent.

sentences.zh: 」兼賜帛三百匹。

translations.literal: " He also granted three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " He also granted him three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，賦斂繁重，伏伽屢奏請改革，高祖並納焉。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many, taxes and levies heavy and numerous; Fujia repeatedly memorialized requesting reforms, and Gaozu accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military and state affairs were pressing and taxes and levies were heavy. Fujia repeatedly memorialized requesting reforms, and Gaozu accepted them all.

sentences.zh: 二年，高祖謂裴寂曰：「隋末無道，上下相蒙，主則驕矜，臣惟諂佞。

translations.literal: In the second year, Gaozu said to Pei Ji: "At the end of Sui the Way was lost; above and below deceived one another; the lord was arrogant, ministers only flattered."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Gaozu said to Pei Ji, "At the end of Sui the Way was lost. Above and below deceived one another: the ruler grew arrogant and his ministers only flattered."

sentences.zh: 上不聞過，下不盡忠，至使社稷傾危，身死匹夫之手。

translations.literal: Above did not hear faults, below did not exhaust loyalty, until the altars of state tilted in peril and he died by the hand of an ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler never heard of his faults, and his subjects never gave their full loyalty, until the altars of state were overturned and he died at the hands of an ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 朕撥亂反正，志在安人，平亂任武臣，守成委文吏，庶得各展器能，以匡不逮。

translations.literal: I dispelled disorder and returned to rectitude, intent on settling the people; pacifying disorder I entrust martial ministers, preserving the accomplishment I delegate to civil officials, hoping each may display their capacity to correct my inadequacies.
translations.idiomatic: I have dispelled chaos and restored order, my aim being to settle the people. In pacifying disorder I rely on martial ministers; in preserving the realm I entrust civil officials, hoping each may display his talents to correct my shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 比每虛心接待，冀聞讜言。

translations.literal: Recently every time I received with empty heart, hoping to hear honest words.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have received everyone with an open mind, hoping to hear honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 然惟李綱善盡忠款，孫伏伽可謂誠直，餘人猶踵弊風，俯首而已，豈朕所望哉！

translations.literal: Yet only Li Gang well exhausts loyal sincerity, Sun Fujia may be called honest and straight; the rest still tread the corrupt wind and only bow their heads—is this what I hope for!
translations.idiomatic: Yet only Li Gang has fully shown loyal sincerity, and Sun Fujia may be called honest and forthright. The rest still follow the corrupt old ways and merely bow their heads—is this what I hoped for!

sentences.zh: 」及平王世充、竇建德，大赦天下，既而責其黨與，並令配遷。

translations.literal: " When Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande were pacified, a great amnesty was proclaimed for the realm; afterward their partisans were blamed and all ordered banished and relocated.
translations.idiomatic: " After Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande were defeated, a general amnesty was proclaimed for the realm. Then their followers were held accountable and all were ordered banished and relocated.

sentences.zh: 伏伽上表諫曰：

translations.literal: Fujia submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fujia submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞王言無戲，自古格言；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard the king's words are not for jest—an ancient maxim since antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a ruler's words are not spoken in jest—this has been a maxim since antiquity;

sentences.zh: 去食存信，聞諸舊典。
