translations.literal: discard food and preserve faith—heard in the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: and that one may give up food but not faith—this is recorded in the ancient canons.

sentences.zh: 故《書》云：「爾無不信，朕不食言。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says: "You must not disbelieve—I do not eat my words."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "You must not disbelieve me—I do not eat my words."

sentences.zh: 」又《論語》雲，一言出口，駟不及舌。

translations.literal: " The Analects also says that when one word leaves the mouth, four horses cannot overtake the tongue.
translations.idiomatic: " The Analects also says that once a word leaves the mouth, not even four horses can overtake the tongue.

sentences.zh: 以此而論，言之出口，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Speaking thus, when words leave the mouth, one cannot but be careful.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that words once spoken cannot be uttered carelessly.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下光臨區宇，覆育群生，率土之濱，誰非臣妾。

translations.literal: Bowing myself before Your Majesty illuminating the realm, covering and nurturing all living beings—along the shores of the land, who is not subject?
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty illuminates the realm and nurtures all living beings. Along the shores of the land, who is not your subject?

sentences.zh: 絲綸一發，取信萬方，使聞之者不疑，見之者不惑。

translations.literal: When silk edict issues once, trust is taken from the myriad regions; let those who hear not doubt, those who see not be confused.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial edict issues forth, it must win trust throughout the realm, so that those who hear it do not doubt and those who see it are not confused.

sentences.zh: 陛下今月二日發雲雨之制，光被黔黎，無所間然，公私蒙賴。

translations.literal: Your Majesty this month on the second day issued the regulation of clouds and rain, its light spread over the blackheads, nothing excluded, public and private alike receiving benefit.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of this month Your Majesty issued a general amnesty, spreading its grace over the common people without exception, to the benefit of public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 既雲常赦不免，皆赦除之，此非直赦其有罪，亦是與天下斷當，許其更新。

translations.literal: Having already said that constant amnesty cannot exempt and all are pardoned and removed—this is not merely pardoning their guilt but also settling accounts with the realm, permitting their renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Having declared that even those normally excluded from amnesty are all pardoned, this is not merely forgiving their crimes but also settling accounts with the realm and permitting them to begin anew.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，但是赦後，即便無事。

translations.literal: Speaking thus, whatever is after the amnesty should straightaway be without affair.
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning, once the amnesty is proclaimed, all should be settled.

sentences.zh: 因何王世充及建德部下，赦後乃欲遷之？

translations.literal: Why then Wang Shichong and Jiande's subordinates, after the amnesty do you wish to relocate them?
translations.idiomatic: Why then do you wish to relocate the followers of Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande after the amnesty?

sentences.zh: 此是陛下自違本心，欲遣下人若為取則？

translations.literal: This is Your Majesty yourself violating your own heart—wishing to send down to the people, how shall they take it as rule?
translations.idiomatic: This is Your Majesty going against your own intent. How are your subjects below to know what rule to follow?

sentences.zh: 若欲子細推尋，逆城之內，人誰無罪？

translations.literal: If you wish carefully to pursue and search, within the rebel cities who is without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to investigate thoroughly, who within the rebel cities is without guilt?

sentences.zh: 故《書》云：「殲厥渠魁，脅從罔治。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says: "Destroy their chieftain; the coerced follow—none punish."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "Destroy their chieftains; as for those coerced into following, do not punish them."

sentences.zh: 」若論渠魁，世充等為首，渠魁尚免，脅從何辜？

translations.literal: " If speaking of chieftains, Shichong and others are the heads; the chieftains are still spared—what guilt have the coerced?
translations.idiomatic: " If we speak of ringleaders, Shichong and the others are the chiefs. If the chiefs are spared, what crime have the coerced committed?

sentences.zh: 且古人云：「蹠狗吠堯，蓋非其主。

translations.literal: And an ancient said: "A Zhi dog barks at Yao—it is not his master."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, an ancient said: "When Zhi's dog barks at Yao, it is because Yao is not its master."

sentences.zh: 」在東都城內及建德部下，乃有與陛下積小故舊，編髮友朋，猶尚有人敗後始至者。

translations.literal: " Within the Eastern Capital city and under Jiande, there were even those with Your Majesty having accumulated small old ties, hair-bound friends, and still some who came only after defeat.
translations.idiomatic: " Within the Eastern Capital and among Jiande's followers there were even men who had old ties with Your Majesty and sworn friends from youth, and some who came only after defeat.

sentences.zh: 此等豈忘陛下，皆云被壅故也。

translations.literal: How could such persons forget Your Majesty? All say they were blocked off, therefore.
translations.idiomatic: How could such men have forgotten Your Majesty? They all say they were cut off from you and had no choice.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，自外疏者，竊謂無罪。

translations.literal: Speaking thus, those distant from outside—I privately say are without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning, I privately hold that those who were distant outsiders are without guilt.

sentences.zh: 又《書》云：「非知之艱，行之惟艱。

translations.literal: Also the Documents says: "Not that knowing is hard—acting is what is hard."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents also says: "It is not knowing that is hard, but acting on it that is hard."

sentences.zh: 」上古以來，何代無君，所以只稱堯、舜之善者，何也？

translations.literal: " From high antiquity, what generation lacked a lord? Therefore only Yao and Shun's goodness are praised—why?
translations.idiomatic: " Since high antiquity, what age has lacked a ruler? Why then are only Yao and Shun praised for their goodness?

sentences.zh: 直由為天子者實難，善名難得故也。

translations.literal: It is directly because being son of Heaven is truly hard and a good name hard to obtain, therefore.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply because being son of Heaven is truly difficult and a good reputation hard to win.

sentences.zh: 往者天下未平，威權須應機而作；

translations.literal: Formerly the realm was not yet settled, awesome authority had to act according to opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when the realm was not yet settled, awesome authority had to be exercised as occasion demanded;

sentences.zh: 今四方既定，設法須與人共之。

translations.literal: now the four quarters are already settled—establishing law must be shared with the people.
translations.idiomatic: now that the four quarters are settled, establishing law must be done in concert with the people.

sentences.zh: 但法者，陛下自作之，還須守之，使天下百姓信而畏之。

translations.literal: But law is what Your Majesty yourself made; you must still keep it, making the people of the realm trust and fear it.
translations.idiomatic: But the law is what Your Majesty yourself established. You must still uphold it so that the people of the realm trust and fear it.

sentences.zh: 今自為無信，欲遣兆人若為信畏？

translations.literal: Now you yourself are without faith—wishing to send down to the myriad people, how will they trust and fear?
translations.idiomatic: If you yourself are faithless now, how can you expect the myriad people to trust and fear you?

sentences.zh: 故《書》云：「無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩；

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says: "Without partiality, without cliques—the kingly Way is vast and ample;"
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "Without partiality, without cliques—the kingly Way is vast and ample;"

sentences.zh: 無黨無偏，王道平平。

translations.literal: without cliques, without partiality—the kingly Way is level and even.
translations.idiomatic: without faction or favoritism—the kingly Way is smooth and fair.

sentences.zh: 」賞罰之行，達乎貴賤，聖人製法，無限親疏。

translations.literal: " Rewards and punishments in their execution reach noble and base; the sage made law without limit of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: " In the application of rewards and punishments, the sage who made the law drew no distinction between noble and base, near and far.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，世充、建德下偽官，經赦合免責情，欲遷配者，請並放之，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: As your servant's foolish view, the false officials under Shichong and Jiande who after amnesty fit exemption from guilt and you wish to relocate—please release them all, then the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, the former officials under Shichong and Jiande who, having been amnestied, ought to be exempt from further punishment but whom you wish to relocate—I ask that they all be released. Then the realm will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 又上表請置諫官，高祖皆納焉。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial requesting establishment of remonstrance officers; Gaozu accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of remonstrance officers, and Gaozu accepted all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，賜爵樂安縣男。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was granted the title Baron of Le'an County.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Fujia was granted the title Baron of Le'an County.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，轉大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗馬射，伏伽上書諫曰：「臣聞千金之子，坐不垂堂；

translations.literal: Taizong once shot on horseback; Fujia submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that the son of a thousand in gold does not sit with his hall lowered;"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once shot on horseback. Fujia submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have heard that the son of a man worth a thousand in gold does not sit beneath a low eave;"

sentences.zh: 百金之子，立不倚衡。

translations.literal: the son of a hundred in gold does not stand leaning on the balustrade.
translations.idiomatic: the son of a man worth a hundred in gold does not stand leaning on a balustrade.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，天下之主，不可履險乘危明矣。

translations.literal: Speaking thus, the lord of the realm must not tread danger and ride peril—how clear!
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the ruler of the realm must not tread danger or court peril—how clear this is!

sentences.zh: 臣又聞天子之居也，則禁衛九重；

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that the son of Heaven's residence has ninefold barred guards;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the son of Heaven's dwelling is guarded by ninefold barriers;

sentences.zh: 其動也，則出警入蹕。

translations.literal: when he moves, troops go out and the imperial guard enters the street cordon.
translations.idiomatic: when he moves, troops go out before him and the imperial guard clears the road.

sentences.zh: 此非極尊其居處，乃為社稷生靈之大計耳。

translations.literal: This is not to exalt his dwelling to the utmost but is the great plan for the altars of state and living souls.
translations.idiomatic: This is not merely to exalt his dwelling to the utmost but is the great plan for the altars of state and the welfare of the people.

sentences.zh: 故古人云：『一人有慶，兆人賴之。

translations.literal: Therefore an ancient said: 'When one man has celebration, the myriad people rely on it.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore an ancient said: 'When one man has cause for celebration, the myriad people rely upon him.'

sentences.zh: 』臣竊聞陛下猶自走馬射帖，娛悅近臣，此乃無禁乘危，竊為陛下有所不取也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately hears Your Majesty still personally gallops horses to shoot at targets, amusing and pleasing close ministers—this is riding danger without prohibition; your servant privately holds that Your Majesty should not take this.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard privately that Your Majesty still personally gallops on horseback to shoot at targets, amusing your close ministers. This is to court danger without restraint, and I privately hold that Your Majesty should not do this.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 一則非光史冊，二則未足顯揚，又非所以導養聖躬，亦不可以垂範後代。

translations.literal: First, it does not glorify the historical records; second, it is insufficient to display and spread; again it is not how to guide and nurture the sacred person, nor can it be handed down as model to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: First, it does not bring glory to the historical records; second, it is insufficient to display your virtue; moreover, it is not how to guide and nurture your sacred person, nor can it serve as a model for later generations.

sentences.zh: 此只是少年諸王之所務，豈得既為天子，今日猶行之乎？

translations.literal: This is only what young princes of the realm pursue—how can one already be son of Heaven and still do it today?
translations.idiomatic: This is only what young princes pursue. How can one who is already son of Heaven still do it today?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲自輕，其奈社稷天下何！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty wishes to treat yourself lightly, what of the altars of state and the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty may wish to treat yourself lightly, what of the altars of state and the realm under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，竊謂不可。

translations.literal: As your servant's foolish view, I privately say it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, I privately hold that this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」太宗覽之大悅。

translations.literal: " Taizong read it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong read it with great delight.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐奏囚誤失免官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for error in reporting prisoners he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was dismissed from office for errors in reporting on prisoners.

sentences.zh: 尋起為刑部郎中，累遷大理少卿，轉民部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored as Director in the Ministry of Justice, repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Judicial Review, transferred to Vice Minister of the People.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as director in the Ministry of Justice, was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and was transferred to vice minister of the people.

sentences.zh: 十四年，拜大理卿，後出為陝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Director of Judicial Review, later sent out as Governor of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed director of the Court of Judicial Review, and later was sent out as governor of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui, on account of old age he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui he retired on account of old age.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Xianqing.

sentences.zh: 張玄素，蒲州虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuansu was a man of Yuxiang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuansu was a native of Yuxiang in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋末，為景城縣戶曹。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he was Household Records Clerk of Jingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui he served as household records clerk of Jingcheng County.

sentences.zh: 竇建德攻陷景城，玄素被執，將就戮，縣民千餘人號泣請代其命，曰：「此人清慎若是，今倘殺之，乃無天也。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande captured Jingcheng; Xuansu was seized and about to be executed; more than a thousand county people wept and begged to die in his stead, saying, "This man's purity and caution are such—if now you kill him, there will be no Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande captured Jingcheng. Xuansu was seized and about to be executed. More than a thousand county people wept and begged to die in his place, saying, "This man is so pure and cautious—if you kill him now, Heaven itself will be gone."

sentences.zh: 大王將定天下，當深加禮接，以招四方，如何殺之，使善人解體？

translations.literal: Great King, about to settle the realm, should deeply add courtesy and reception to attract the four quarters—how kill him and make good men lose heart?
translations.idiomatic: Great King, as you are about to settle the realm, you should treat such men with deep courtesy to win men from every quarter. How can you kill him and make good men lose heart?

sentences.zh: 」建德遽命釋之，署為治書侍御史，固辭不受。

translations.literal: " Jiande promptly ordered him released, appointed him Imperial Censor, but he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiande promptly ordered him released and appointed him imperial censor, but he firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 及江都不守，又召拜黃門侍郎，始應命。

translations.literal: When Jiangdu fell, he was again summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and only then answered the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangdu fell, he was again summoned and appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate, and only then accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 建德平，授景城都督府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Jiande was pacified, he was appointed Record-Keeping Aide of the Jingcheng Area Command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande was defeated, he was appointed record-keeping aide of the Jingcheng area command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，及即位，召見，訪以政道。

translations.literal: Taizong heard his name; when he took the throne he summoned and received him, inquiring about the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had heard his name. When he took the throne he summoned Xuansu, received him in audience, and inquired about the way of government.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣觀自古以來，未有如隋室喪亂之甚，豈非其君自專，其法日亂。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant observes that from antiquity until now there has been none like the Sui house in the extremity of disorder and ruin—is it not that its lord acted alone and its laws daily fell into chaos?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I observe that from antiquity until now there has been nothing like the disorder and ruin of the Sui house. Was this not because its ruler acted alone and its laws fell daily into chaos?"

sentences.zh: 向使君虛受於上，臣弼違於下，豈至於此？

translations.literal: If only the lord had received with emptiness above and ministers assisted and remonstrated below, how would it have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: If only the ruler had received counsel openly above and his ministers had assisted and remonstrated below, how could it have come to this?

sentences.zh: 且萬乘之重，又欲自專庶務，日斷十事而五條不中，中者信善，其如不中者何？

translations.literal: Moreover, the weight of ten thousand chariots—yet also wishing to monopolize petty affairs oneself, deciding ten matters a day while five clauses miss the mark; those that hit may indeed be good, but what of those that do not hit?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the burden of ruling the realm is immense—yet if you also wish to monopolize every petty affair yourself, deciding ten cases a day while five go wrong, those you get right may indeed be sound, but what of the ones you get wrong?

sentences.zh: 況一日萬機，己多虧失，以日繼月，乃至累年，乖謬既多，不亡何待！

translations.literal: How much more when in one day ten thousand mechanisms—already many losses; day following month, even to accumulated years—aberrations already numerous; if not perishing, what waits?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the myriad affairs of state in a single day already bring many failures—and day by day, month by month, even year after year, the errors mount. With so many mistakes, how can ruin not follow?

sentences.zh: 如其廣任賢良，高居深視，百司奉職，誰敢犯之？

translations.literal: If you broadly entrust worthy and good men, sit high and look deeply, the hundred offices hold to their duties—who would dare violate it?
translations.idiomatic: If you broadly entrust worthy men, hold yourself aloof and observe deeply, and let the hundred offices perform their duties—who would dare transgress?

sentences.zh: 臣又觀隋末沸騰，被於宇縣，所爭天下者不過十數人，余皆保邑全身，思歸有道。

translations.literal: Your servant again observes that at the end of Sui turmoil boiled, extending over the realm; those contending for the realm were no more than a dozen or so men—the rest all preserved their towns and kept their persons whole, thinking to return to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I have also observed that at the end of Sui turmoil surged throughout the realm. Those who contended for the empire were no more than a dozen men; the rest all guarded their towns and preserved themselves, longing to return to the right Way.

sentences.zh: 是知人欲背主為亂者鮮矣，但人君不能安之，遂致於亂。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that those wishing to turn against their lord and make chaos are few—but the lord cannot settle them, and so it comes to chaos.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that few people truly wish to rebel against their lord; it is only that rulers cannot keep them content, and chaos ensues.

sentences.zh: 陛下若近覽危亡，日慎一日，堯、舜之道，何以能加！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty closely surveys peril and ruin, daily cautious one day more—how could Yao and Shun's Way be added to!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty closely heeds the lessons of ruin and grows more cautious day by day, how could even the Way of Yao and Shun surpass you!

sentences.zh: 」太宗善其對，擢拜侍御史，尋遷給事中。

translations.literal: " Taizong approved his reply, promoted and appointed him Attendant Censor, shortly transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong approved his reply, promoted him to attendant censor, and shortly transferred him to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，詔發卒修洛陽宮乾陽殿，以備巡幸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, an edict issued to mobilize corvée to repair the Qianyang Hall of the Luoyang Palace, to prepare for imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, an edict was issued to mobilize laborers to repair the Qianyang Hall of the Luoyang Palace in preparation for imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 玄素上書諫曰：

translations.literal: Xuansu submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 微臣竊思秦始皇之為君也，藉周室之餘、六國之盛，將貽之萬葉，及其子而亡，良由逞嗜奔欲，逆天害人者也。

translations.literal: Your humble servant privately reflects on the First Emperor of Qin as lord: relying on the Zhou house's remainder and the Six States' grandeur, he would bequeath it to ten thousand generations—yet before his son it perished, truly because he gave free rein to cravings and rushed after desires, going against Heaven and harming men.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant reflects that the First Emperor of Qin, as ruler, built on the remnants of the Zhou and the power of the Six States, intending to bequeath his empire for ten thousand generations—yet it fell before his son did, truly because he indulged every craving and desire, defying Heaven and harming his people.

sentences.zh: 是知天下不可以力勝，神祇不可以親恃，惟當弘儉約，薄賦斂，慎終如始，可以永固。

translations.literal: Thus one knows the realm cannot be overcome by force, the spirits cannot be relied on through closeness—only by expanding frugality, lightening taxes and levies, and being careful at the end as at the beginning can it be forever secured.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the realm cannot be won by force alone, nor can the spirits be trusted through personal favor—only by promoting frugality, lightening taxes and levies, and remaining as careful at the end as at the beginning can the empire endure.

sentences.zh: 方今承百王之末，屬凋弊之餘，必欲節之以禮制，陛下宜以身為先。

translations.literal: Now inheriting the end of a hundred kings, belonging to the remainder of decline and ruin—if you must regulate it with ritual and institutions, Your Majesty should take the body as first.
translations.idiomatic: Now you inherit the legacy of a hundred kings and rule over a people exhausted by decline. If you wish to restrain excess through ritual and institutions, Your Majesty should set the example yourself.

sentences.zh: 東都未有幸期，即何須補葺？

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital has no date of fortunate arrival—why then need repair and patch?
translations.idiomatic: You have not yet set a date to visit the Eastern Capital—why then need repairs?

sentences.zh: 諸王今並出籓，又須營構，興發漸多，豈疲人之所望？

translations.literal: The various princes now all go out to their fiefs and again must build and construct; mobilizations gradually increase—how is this what the weary people hope for?
translations.idiomatic: The princes have all gone out to their fiefs and must build residences there as well. Public works are multiplying—is this what your exhausted people hope for?

sentences.zh: 其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 陛下初平東都之始，層樓廣殿，皆令撤毀，天下翕然，同心欣仰。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first pacified the Eastern Capital, tiered towers and broad halls were all ordered dismantled; the realm was of one accord, hearts united in joyful admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first pacified the Eastern Capital, you ordered tiered towers and vast halls dismantled. The realm was united in joyful admiration.

sentences.zh: 豈有初則惡其侈靡，今乃襲其雕麗？

translations.literal: How can there be at first hating its extravagance, now yet following its carved splendor?
translations.idiomatic: How can you at first have condemned its extravagance and now adopt its ornate splendor?

sentences.zh: 其不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 每承音旨，未即巡幸，此則事不急之務，成虛費之勞。

translations.literal: Every time receiving your gracious command, you do not immediately tour—this then is an affair not urgent, becoming empty expenditure and toil.
translations.idiomatic: Each time you receive reports, you do not immediately tour the east. This is not an urgent matter, yet it becomes wasted labor and expense.

sentences.zh: 國無兼年之積，何用兩都之好，勞役過度，怨讟將起。

translations.literal: The state has no surplus of two years' store—what use the fondness for two capitals? Corvée labor excessive, resentment and slander about to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The state lacks even two years' surplus in its granaries—what need is there to favor two capitals? With corvée labor excessive, resentment and complaint will soon arise.

sentences.zh: 其不可三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 百姓承亂離之後，財力凋盡，天恩含育，粗見存立，飢寒猶切，生計未安，三五年間，恐未平復。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames, inheriting after disorder and separation, wealth and strength withered to exhaustion; Heaven's grace contains and nurtures them, roughly seeing preservation—hunger and cold still pressing, livelihood not yet settled; within three or five years, I fear not yet restored.
translations.idiomatic: The people, after years of chaos and separation, have seen their wealth exhausted. Though Heaven's grace has preserved them, hunger and cold still press upon them and their livelihoods are not yet secure. Within three or five years they may not yet recover.

sentences.zh: 奈何營未幸之都，奪疲人之力？

translations.literal: How can you build a capital not yet visited and seize the strength of the weary people?
translations.idiomatic: How can you build up a capital you have not yet visited and strip the strength from your exhausted people?

sentences.zh: 其不可四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖將都洛陽，婁敬一言，即日西駕，豈不知地惟土中，貢賦所均，但以形勝不如關內也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han was about to make the capital at Luoyang; Lou Jing's one word, and that very day he drove west—did he not know the land was the center of earth and tribute evenly distributed? Only that strategic advantage was not like within the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han was about to establish his capital at Luoyang, but Lou Jing spoke one word and that very day the emperor turned west. Did he not know that Luoyang lies at the center of the realm where tribute is evenly distributed? He knew—but its strategic advantage was inferior to that within the Pass.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下化凋弊之人，革澆漓之俗，為日尚淺，未甚淳和。

translations.literal: Bowing myself before Your Majesty transforming people of decline and ruin, reforming the diluted and dissolute custom—days as ruler still shallow, not yet very pure and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty is transforming a people exhausted by decline and reforming dissolute customs, but your reign is still young and society not yet fully restored to harmony.

sentences.zh: 斟酌事宜，詎可東幸？

translations.literal: Weighing affairs as they fit—how can you tour east?
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the circumstances, how can you tour east now?

sentences.zh: 其不可五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 臣又嘗見隋室造殿，楹棟宏壯，大木非隨近所有，多從豫章采來。

translations.literal: Your servant has also once seen the Sui house build halls: pillars and beams vast and strong; great timbers not available nearby, mostly gathered from Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: I have also seen the Sui build their halls: pillars and beams vast and strong, great timbers not available nearby but gathered from distant Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 二千人曳一柱，其下施轂，皆以生鐵為之，若用木輪，便即火出。

translations.literal: Two thousand men dragged one pillar; beneath it wheels were fitted, all made of raw iron—if wooden wheels were used, fire would immediately break out.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand men dragged a single pillar; wheels were fitted beneath, all cast of raw iron—for if wooden wheels were used, friction would set them ablaze.

sentences.zh: 鐵轂既生，行一二里即有破壞，仍數百人別齎鐵轂以隨之，終日不過進三二十里。

translations.literal: The iron wheels being raw, after going one or two li they would break; still several hundred men separately carried iron wheels to follow along—all day they advanced no more than thirty or twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: The raw iron wheels would break after a mile or two, and several hundred men had to carry spare wheels alongside. In a full day they advanced no more than twenty or thirty li.

sentences.zh: 略計一柱，已用數十萬功，則余費又過於此。

translations.literal: Roughly calculating one pillar, already used several hundred thousand work-units—then the remaining expense again exceeded this.
translations.idiomatic: A single pillar alone consumed several hundred thousand man-days of labor—and the remaining costs exceeded even that.

sentences.zh: 臣聞阿房成，秦人散；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: when Epang was completed, the Qin people scattered;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Epang Palace was completed, the Qin people scattered;

sentences.zh: 章華就，楚眾離；

translations.literal: when Zhanghua was finished, the Chu masses departed;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhanghua Terrace was finished, the Chu people dispersed;

sentences.zh: 及乾陽畢功，隋人解體。

translations.literal: when Qianyang was completed in work, the Sui people dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: and when Qianyang Hall was completed, the Sui dynasty fell apart.

sentences.zh: 且以陛下今時功力，何如隋日？

translations.literal: Moreover, comparing Your Majesty's present-time strength and resources, how do they compare to Sui's day?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, comparing Your Majesty's present resources with those of the Sui—how do they compare?

sentences.zh: 役瘡痍之人，襲亡隋之弊，以此言之，恐甚於煬帝。

translations.literal: Employing people covered in sores and wounds, following the fallen Sui's abuses—speaking thus, I fear worse than Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: To employ a people covered in wounds and repeat the abuses that destroyed the Sui—by this reasoning, I fear you may prove worse than Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 深願陛下思之，無為由余所笑，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I deeply wish Your Majesty to reflect on this, not to be laughed at by You Yu—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply urge Your Majesty to reflect on this and not become a laughingstock like You Yu of Qin—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「卿謂我不如煬帝，何如桀、紂？

translations.literal: Taizong said: "You say I am not equal to Emperor Yang—how about Jie and Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "You say I am no better than Emperor Yang—how do I compare with Jie and Zhou?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「若此殿卒興，所謂同歸於亂。

translations.literal: " He replied: "If this hall is hurriedly raised, it is what is called returning together to chaos."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "If this hall is built to completion, we shall all alike return to chaos."

sentences.zh: 且陛下初平東都，太上皇敕大殿高門並宜焚燬，陛下以瓦木可用，不宜焚灼，請賜與貧人。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty first pacified the Eastern Capital, the retired emperor ordered great halls and high gates all to be burned; Your Majesty, because tiles and timber could be used, said they should not be burned and requested they be given to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Your Majesty first pacified the Eastern Capital, the retired emperor ordered the great halls and high gates burned. Your Majesty said the tiles and timber could still be used and should not be burned, and asked that they be given to the poor.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，然天下翕然謳歌至德。

translations.literal: The affair though not carried out, yet the realm was of one accord, singing praise of utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Though the matter was not carried out, the realm was united in singing praise of your supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 今若遵舊制，即是隋役復興。

translations.literal: Now if you follow the old system, this is the Sui corvée revived.
translations.idiomatic: If you now follow the old ways, you will revive the corvée labor of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 五六年間，趨舍頓異，何以昭示子孫，光敷四海？

translations.literal: Within five or six years, direction and dwelling suddenly differ—how can you show and declare to sons and grandsons, spread light over the four seas?
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years your conduct has changed so sharply—how can you show this to your descendants or spread your glory across the four seas?

sentences.zh: 」太宗嘆曰：「我不思量，遂至於此。

translations.literal: " Taizong sighed and said: "I did not think it through, and so it came to this."
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong sighed and said, "I did not think it through, and so it came to this."

sentences.zh: 」顧謂房玄齡曰：「洛陽土中，朝貢道均，朕故修營，意在便於百姓。

translations.literal: " He turned and said to Fang Xuanling: "Luoyang is the center of earth; court tribute roads are even—I therefore repair and build, intent on convenience for the hundred surnames."
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to Fang Xuanling and said, "Luoyang lies at the center of the realm where tribute routes converge. I undertook these repairs intending to benefit the people."

sentences.zh: 今玄素上表，實亦可依，後必事理須行，露坐亦復何苦，所有作役，宜即停之。

translations.literal: Now Xuansu's submitted memorial can truly also be followed; later when affairs and reason must be carried out, sitting in the open will again be what hardship? All corvée work should immediately be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu's memorial can truly be followed. When the time comes and the matter must proceed, what hardship is there in sitting in the open air? All construction labor should be stopped at once.

sentences.zh: 然以卑干尊，古來不易，非其忠直，安能若此？

translations.literal: Yet for the lowly to remonstrate the exalted, since antiquity not easy—were it not for his loyal straightness, how could he be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for the lowly to remonstrate with the exalted has never been easy. Were it not for his loyal forthrightness, how could he have spoken thus?

sentences.zh: 可賜彩二百匹。

translations.literal: He may be granted two hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him two hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 」侍中魏徵嘆曰：「張公論事，遂有回天之力，可謂仁人之言，其利博哉！

translations.literal: " Attendant-in-chief Wei Zheng sighed and said: "Master Zhang's discussing affairs thus has power to turn back Heaven—truly the words of a benevolent man; how broad their benefit!"
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Attendant Wei Zheng sighed and said, "Master Zhang's remonstrance had the power to turn back Heaven itself—truly the words of a benevolent man, and how far-reaching their benefit!"

sentences.zh: 」累遷太子少詹事，轉右庶子。

translations.literal: " He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent, transferred to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: " He was repeatedly promoted to junior steward of the heir apparent and transferred to right vice director of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 時承乾居春宮，頗以游畋廢學，玄素上書諫曰：「臣聞皇天無親，惟德是輔，苟違天道，人神同棄。

translations.literal: At that time Chengqian dwelt in the Eastern Palace and largely abandoned study for roaming and hunting; Xuansu submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that August Heaven has no favorites—only virtue is assisted; if one violates Heaven's Way, men and spirits alike abandon him."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chengqian lived in the Eastern Palace and largely neglected his studies for hunting and pleasure. Xuansu submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have heard that August Heaven shows no partiality and assists only the virtuous. Whoever violates the Way of Heaven is abandoned by both men and spirits alike."

sentences.zh: 然古三驅之禮，非欲教殺，將為百姓除害，故湯羅一面，天下歸仁。

translations.literal: Yet the ancient ritual of three drives was not wishing to teach killing but would remove harm for the hundred surnames; therefore Tang netted on three sides, and the realm returned to benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ancient ritual of the three drives was not meant to teach killing but to rid the people of pests. Thus when Tang left one side of the net open, the realm submitted to his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 今苑中娛獵，雖名異游畋，若行之無常，終虧雅度。

translations.literal: Now hunting for pleasure in the park, though named different from roaming and hunting—if practiced without constancy, in the end it will diminish elegant measure.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting for pleasure in the park, though called something other than roaming and hunting, if practiced without restraint will in the end diminish your noble bearing.

sentences.zh: 且傅說曰：『學不師古，匪說攸聞。

translations.literal: Moreover Fu Yue said: 'Learning without taking antiquity as teacher—this is not what Fu Yue has heard.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Fu Yue said, 'Learning without taking antiquity as one's teacher is something I have never heard of.'

sentences.zh: 』然則弘道在於學古，學古必資師訓。

translations.literal: ' Thus expanding the Way lies in learning antiquity; learning antiquity must rely on teacher's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thus to spread the Way one must study antiquity, and to study antiquity one must rely on teachers.

sentences.zh: 既奉恩詔，令孔穎達侍講，望數存問，以補萬一。

translations.literal: Having received the gracious edict appointing Kong Yingda to attend and lecture, I hope you will frequently inquire after him, to supplement the one in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: You have received the gracious edict appointing Kong Yingda to lecture you. I hope you will frequently seek his instruction, to gain even the smallest benefit.

sentences.zh: 仍博遣有名行學士，兼朝夕侍奉。

translations.literal: Still broadly send famous men of conduct and learning, together attending morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Also send broadly men of renowned conduct and learning to attend you morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 覽聖人之遺教，察既行之往事，日知其所不足，月無忘其所能。

translations.literal: Peruse the sages' transmitted teachings, examine deeds already done in past affairs—daily know what you lack, monthly forget not what you can do.
translations.idiomatic: Read the teachings left by the sages and examine deeds already done in history—daily recognize what you lack, and monthly forget not what you have mastered.

sentences.zh: 此則盡善盡美，夏啟、周誦，焉足言哉！

translations.literal: This then is utmost goodness and utmost beauty—Xia Qi and Zhou Song, how are they worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: By this you would attain the utmost in goodness and beauty—how then could Xia Qi and King Song of Zhou be worth mentioning!

sentences.zh: 夫為人上者，未有不求其善，但以性不勝情，耽惑成亂。

translations.literal: For one who is lord over others, none does not seek his goodness—only that nature cannot overcome emotion, indulgence and delusion become chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stand above others all wish to do good—but when nature cannot master passion, indulgence and delusion lead to disorder.

sentences.zh: 耽惑既甚，忠言遂塞，所以臣下苟順，君道漸虧。

translations.literal: When indulgence and delusion are extreme, loyal words are blocked—therefore ministers below comply in perfunctory fashion and the lord's Way gradually declines.
translations.idiomatic: When indulgence grows extreme, loyal counsel is shut out; ministers merely comply, and the ruler's Way gradually declines.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『勿以小惡而不去，小善而不為。

translations.literal: An ancient said: 'Do not commit a small evil because it is small; do not fail to do a small good because it is small.'
translations.idiomatic: An ancient said, 'Do not commit a small evil because it is small; do not fail to do a small good because it is small.'

sentences.zh: 』故知禍福之來，皆起於漸。

translations.literal: ' Thus one knows fortune and calamity in their coming all arise from the gradual.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thus we know that fortune and calamity alike arise from gradual beginnings.

sentences.zh: 殿下地居儲兩，當須廣樹嘉猷。

translations.literal: Your Highness, dwelling in the storehouse of the two [capitals], must broadly plant fine plans.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness, as heir to the throne, must broadly cultivate worthy policies.

sentences.zh: 既有好畋之淫，何以主斯匕鬯？

translations.literal: Already having the excess of loving the hunt—how can you preside over these sacrificial ladles and libations?
translations.idiomatic: If you indulge in hunting, how can you preside over the ancestral sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 慎終如始，猶懼漸衰，始尚不慎，終將安保！

translations.literal: Being careful at the end as at the beginning, still fearing gradual decline—if at the start you are not yet careful, in the end how will you be secure!
translations.idiomatic: Even when careful at the end as at the beginning one still fears gradual decline—if you are not careful at the start, how can you be secure at the end!

sentences.zh: 」尋又兼太子少詹事。

translations.literal: " Before long he also concurrently served as Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he also concurrently served as junior steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又上書諫曰：「臣聞周公以大聖之材，猶握髮吐飧，引納白屋，而況後之聖賢，敢輕斯道？

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he again submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that the Duke of Zhou, with the talent of a great sage, still grasped his hair and spat out his meal, drawing in men from thatched cottages—how much more later sages and worthies: who would dare treat this Way lightly?"
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he again submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have heard that the Duke of Zhou, though possessed of the talent of a great sage, still would grasp his disheveled hair and spit out his food to receive men from humble cottages—how much more should later sages and worthies dare treat this Way lightly?"

sentences.zh: 是以禮制皇太子入學而行齒胄，欲使太子知君臣、父子、長幼之道。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual institutions have the crown prince enter school and perform the cap-and-girdle ceremony, wishing to make the heir know the Way of lord and minister, father and son, elder and younger.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ritual prescribes that the crown prince enter school and perform the coming-of-age ceremony, so that the heir may learn the ways of ruler and minister, father and son, and elder and younger.

sentences.zh: 然君臣之義、父子之親、尊卑之序、長幼之節，用之方寸之內，弘之四海之外，皆因行以遠聞，假言以光被。

translations.literal: Yet the righteousness of lord and minister, the intimacy of father and son, the order of noble and base, the propriety of elder and younger—applied within a square inch, spread beyond the four seas—all rely on conduct to be heard afar and borrow words to shine abroad.
translations.idiomatic: The duties between ruler and minister, the bond between father and son, the order of rank, and the propriety between elder and younger—applied in one's inner self and extended beyond the four seas—are all made known through conduct and spread through words.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下睿質已隆，尚須學文以飾其表。

translations.literal: Bowing myself before Your Highness, your keen quality is already lofty—still you must study letters to adorn the exterior.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Highness's keen intelligence is already lofty, yet you must still study the classics to adorn your outward bearing.

sentences.zh: 至如孔穎達、趙弘智等，非惟宿德鴻儒，亦兼達政要，望令數得侍講，開釋物理，覽古諭今，增暉睿德。

translations.literal: As for Kong Yingda, Zhao Hongzhi, and the like—not only old in virtue and great Confucians, they also comprehend the essentials of government; I hope you will order them frequently to attend and lecture, opening and explaining the patterns of things, surveying antiquity to instruct the present, adding radiance to your keen virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Kong Yingda and Zhao Hongzhi are not only men of long-standing virtue and great learning but also understand the essentials of government. I hope you will have them lecture you frequently, explain the principles of things, survey antiquity to instruct the present, and add luster to your enlightened virtue.

sentences.zh: 而彫蟲小伎之流，只可時命追隨，以代博弈耳。

translations.literal: But the stream of decorative-insect petty skills may only be summoned at times to follow along, to replace gambling and gaming.
translations.idiomatic: Men skilled only in ornamental arts may be summoned from time to time for amusement, to replace gambling and games.

sentences.zh: 若其騎射畋游，酣歌戲玩，以悅耳目，終穢心神，漸染既久，必移情性。

translations.literal: If you ride, shoot, hunt, roam, sing drunkenly, and play for amusement to please ear and eye—in the end you defile the spirit and mind; gradual staining over long time will surely shift disposition and nature.
translations.idiomatic: But if you devote yourself to riding, archery, hunting, roaming, drunken song, and play to please the senses, you will in the end corrupt your spirit. Long indulgence will surely alter your character.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『心為萬事主，動而無節即亂。

translations.literal: An ancient said: 'The heart is master of the myriad things; movement without measure is chaos.'
translations.idiomatic: An ancient said, 'The heart is master of all things; movement without restraint is chaos.'

sentences.zh: 』臣恐殿下敗德之源，在於此矣。

translations.literal: ' Your servant fears the source of Your Highness's lost virtue lies here.
translations.idiomatic: ' I fear the source of Your Highness's moral decline lies here.

sentences.zh: 」承乾並不能納。

translations.literal: " Chengqian could not accept any of it.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengqian would accept none of it.

sentences.zh: 太宗知玄素在東宮頻有進諫，十四年，擢授銀青光祿大夫，行太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Taizong knew Xuansu in the Eastern Palace frequently offered advancing remonstrance; in the fourteenth year he was promoted and granted Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting as Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong knew that Xuansu in the Eastern Palace had frequently offered remonstrance. In the fourteenth year he was promoted to silver radiance grand master of splendid happiness and appointed acting left vice director of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 時承乾久不坐朝，玄素諫曰：「宮內止有婦人耳，不知如樊姬之徒，可與弘益聖德者有幾？

translations.literal: At that time Chengqian long did not attend court; Xuansu remonstrated: "Within the palace there are only women—one does not know how many like Fan Ji can enlarge and benefit sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chengqian had long ceased attending court. Xuansu remonstrated, "Within the palace there are only women. One wonders how many like Fan Ji there are who can enlarge and benefit your sagely virtue."

sentences.zh: 若遂無賢哲，便是親嬖倖，遠忠良。

translations.literal: If in the end there are no worthy and wise, this is being close to favorites and keeping loyal and good at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: If there are no worthy and wise at all, you are drawing close to favorites and keeping the loyal and good at a distance.

sentences.zh: 人不見德，何以光敷三善？

translations.literal: If men do not see virtue, how can you spread light over the three excellences?
translations.idiomatic: If men do not see your virtue, how can you spread the light of the three excellences?

sentences.zh: 且宮儲之寄，於國為重，所以廣置群僚，以輔睿德。

translations.literal: Moreover the charge of the palace heir is heavy for the state; therefore a broad array of officials is set to assist keen virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the charge of the crown prince is weighty for the state; therefore many officials are appointed to assist your enlightened virtue.

sentences.zh: 今乃動經時月，不見宮臣，納誨既疏，將何補闕？

translations.literal: Now for months on end you do not see palace officials; receiving admonition already sparse—how will you remedy oversights?
translations.idiomatic: Now months pass without your seeing palace officials. Counsel is already sparse—how will you remedy your shortcomings?

sentences.zh: 」承乾嫉其數諫，遣戶奴夜以馬撾擊之，殆至於死。

translations.literal: " Chengqian resented his repeated remonstrance and sent a household slave by night to strike him with a horse whip, nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengqian resented his repeated remonstrance and sent a household slave by night to beat him with a horse whip, nearly killing him.

sentences.zh: 承乾又嘗於宮中擊鼓，聲聞於外，玄素叩閣請見，極言切諫，承乾乃出宮內鼓，對玄素毀之。

translations.literal: Chengqian also once beat drums within the palace, the sound heard outside; Xuansu knocked at the gate and requested audience, speaking remonstrance with utmost urgency; Chengqian then brought out the palace drums and destroyed them before Xuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian also once beat drums within the palace until the sound was heard outside. Xuansu knocked at the gate and requested audience, remonstrating with utmost urgency. Chengqian then brought out the palace drums and destroyed them before Xuansu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太宗嘗對朝問玄素歷官所由，玄素既出自刑部令史，甚以慚恥。

translations.literal: That year Taizong once at court asked Xuansu the course of his official posts; Xuansu, having come from a clerk in the Ministry of Justice, was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizong once asked Xuansu at court about the course of his official career. Xuansu, having begun as a clerk in the Ministry of Justice, was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良上疏曰：「臣聞君子不失言於人，聖主不戲言於臣。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the gentleman does not speak lightly to others, and the sage lord does not jest in words to ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and counsel grandee Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial: "I have heard that a gentleman does not speak lightly to others, and a sage ruler does not jest with his ministers."

sentences.zh: 言則史書之，禮成之，樂歌之。

translations.literal: When he speaks, the historians record it; when ritual is completed, they complete it; music sings it.
translations.idiomatic: When he speaks, the historians record it; when ritual is performed, it is enacted; when music is made, it is sung.

sentences.zh: 居上能禮其臣，臣始能盡力以奉其上。

translations.literal: When the superior can treat his ministers with ritual, ministers then can exhaust their strength to serve their superior.
translations.idiomatic: When the superior can treat his ministers with courtesy, ministers can then exhaust their strength in his service.

sentences.zh: 近代宋孝武輕言肆口，侮弄朝臣，攻其門戶，乃至狼狽。

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Xiaowu of Song spoke lightly and freely, insulted and toyed with court ministers, attacked their households and lineages, even to disheveled distress.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Emperor Xiaowu of Song spoke lightly and freely, insulted and toyed with court ministers, and attacked their family backgrounds, even to their utter humiliation.

sentences.zh: 良史書之，以為非是。

translations.literal: Good historians recorded it and held it not right.
translations.idiomatic: Good historians recorded this and judged it wrong.

sentences.zh: 陛下昨見問張玄素云：『隋任何官？

translations.literal: Your Majesty yesterday was seen questioning Zhang Xuansu, saying: 'What office did he hold under Sui?'
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Your Majesty was seen questioning Zhang Xuansu, saying, 'What office did he hold under the Sui?'

sentences.zh: 』奏云：『縣尉。

translations.literal: ' He replied: 'County vice-magistrate.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He answered, 'County vice-magistrate.'

sentences.zh: 』又問：『未為縣尉已前？

translations.literal: ' Again asked: 'Before becoming county vice-magistrate?'
translations.idiomatic: ' You asked again, 'Before he became county vice-magistrate?'

sentences.zh: 』奏云：『流外。

translations.literal: ' He replied: 'Outside the regular stream.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He answered, 'Outside the regular stream.'

sentences.zh: 』又問：『在何曹司？

translations.literal: ' Again asked: 'In what bureau and office?'
translations.idiomatic: ' You asked again, 'In what bureau and office?'

sentences.zh: 』玄素將出閣門，殆不能移步，精爽頓盡，色類死灰。

translations.literal: ' Xuansu was about to leave the gate of the pavilion, barely able to move his steps; his spirit and clarity suddenly exhausted, his color like dead ashes.
translations.idiomatic: ' As Xuansu was about to leave the gate of the pavilion, he could barely walk. His spirit was utterly crushed and his face was the color of dead ashes.

sentences.zh: 朝臣見之，多所驚怪。

translations.literal: Court ministers who saw it were mostly startled and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers who saw this were mostly startled and astonished.

sentences.zh: 大唐創歷，任官以才；

translations.literal: Great Tang founded the calendar, appointing officials by talent;
translations.idiomatic: Great Tang founded its dynasty and appoints officials by talent;

sentences.zh: 卜祝庸保，量能使用。

translations.literal: Diviners, prayer-officers, menials, and guards—measure capacity and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners, prayer-officers, menials, and guards were appointed according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 陛下禮重玄素，頻年任使，擢授三品，翼贊皇儲，自不可更對群臣，窮其門戶，棄昔日之殊恩，成一朝之愧恥。

translations.literal: Your Majesty honors Xuansu with ritual, repeatedly over years employs him, promoted and granted third rank, assists and supports the imperial heir—by nature one cannot again face the host of ministers, exhaust his household and lineage, cast aside former special grace, and make a morning's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has honored Xuansu with ceremony, employed him repeatedly over the years, promoted him to the third rank, and entrusted him to assist the crown prince. You surely cannot now question him before the whole court, pry into his family background, cast aside your former special favor, and turn a single morning into humiliation.

sentences.zh: 人君之御臣下也，禮義以導之，惠澤以驅之，使其負戴玄天，罄輸臣節，猶恐德禮不加，人不自勵。

translations.literal: When a lord rules his ministers below, he guides them with ritual and righteousness, drives them with favor and grace, making them bear and uphold the dark Heaven and exhaust their ministerial devotion—yet still fears virtue and ritual are not added and men do not urge themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler governs his ministers, he should guide them with ritual and righteousness and inspire them with favor and grace, so that they bear up the realm and give their full loyalty. Even then he may still fear that without added virtue and courtesy men will not strive of themselves.

sentences.zh: 若無故忽略，使其羞慚，鬱結於懷，衷心靡樂，責其伏節死義，其可得乎？

translations.literal: If without cause you neglect him, making him ashamed, knotted in the breast, his loyal heart without joy—requiring him to submit his integrity and die for righteousness, how can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If without cause you slight him and fill him with shame, so that grief knots in his breast and his loyal heart knows no joy, how can you then demand that he lay down his life in loyal service?

sentences.zh: 」書奏，太宗謂遂良曰：「朕亦悔此問，今得卿疏，深會我心。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted. Taizong said to Suiliang: "I too regret this question. Now receiving your memorial, it deeply meets my heart."
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, Taizong said to Suiliang, "I too regret having asked this. Your memorial now reaches the very heart of the matter."

sentences.zh: 」承乾既敗德日增，玄素又上書諫曰：

translations.literal: " Chengqian's lost virtue daily increased; Xuansu again submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " As Chengqian's conduct worsened day by day, Xuansu again submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞孔子云：「能近取譬，可謂仁之方也已。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard Confucius say: "Able to take comparisons from what is near—this may be called the method of humaneness."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard Confucius say, "If one can draw comparisons from what is near at hand, that may be called the method of humaneness."

sentences.zh: 」然《書》、《傳》所載，言之或遠，尋覽近事，得失斯存。

translations.literal: " Yet what the Documents and Traditions record sometimes speaks from afar; searching recent affairs, gain and loss are preserved therein.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet what the Classics and commentaries record sometimes speaks of distant ages. If we examine recent events, the lessons of success and failure lie before us.

sentences.zh: 至如周武帝平定山東，卑宮菲食，以安海內。

translations.literal: Take for example Emperor Wu of Zhou pacifying the east of the mountains, low palaces and meager food, to settle the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Emperor Wu of Zhou, who pacified the east, lived in humble quarters and ate plain food, and thereby brought peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 太子贇舉措無端，穢德日著。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yun's conduct and movements were without reason; foul virtue daily grew conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: His crown prince Yun behaved without restraint, and his debased conduct grew more notorious day by day.

sentences.zh: 烏九軌知其不可，具言於武帝；

translations.literal: Wu Jiugui knew he could not be allowed to continue and fully spoke to Emperor Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui saw that this could not continue and spoke frankly to Emperor Wu;

sentences.zh: 武帝慈仁，望其漸改。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was kind and benevolent, hoping he would gradually reform.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, being kind and benevolent, hoped the prince would gradually reform.

sentences.zh: 及至踐祚，狂暴肆情，區宇崩離，宗祀覆滅，即隋文帝所代是也。

translations.literal: When he came to tread the throne, violent and wild, indulging his passions, the realm collapsed and separated, the ancestral sacrifices overturned and destroyed—this is what Emperor Wen of Sui replaced.
translations.idiomatic: But when Yun ascended the throne he grew violent and unrestrained, the realm split apart, and the Zhou house was destroyed—the very dynasty that Emperor Wen of Sui overthrew.

sentences.zh: 文帝因周衰弱，憑藉女資，雖無大功於天下，然布德行仁，足為萬姓所賴。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because Zhou was weak and declining, relied on his wife's resources; though without great merit toward the realm, yet he spread virtue and practiced humaneness, enough for the myriad clans to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen rose when Zhou was weak and relied on his marriage alliance. Though he won no great victories, he spread virtue and practiced benevolence, and the people could rely on him.

sentences.zh: 勇為太子，不能近遵君父之節儉，而務驕侈，今之山池遺蹟，即殿下所親睹是也。

translations.literal: Yong as crown prince could not closely follow his lord-father's frugality but devoted himself to arrogance and extravagance; today's mountain pools and surviving traces are what Your Highness has personally seen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong, as crown prince, would not follow his father's frugality but pursued arrogance and luxury. The ruined hills and pools you can still see today are what Your Highness has witnessed with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 此時亦恃君親之恩，自謂太山之固，詎知邪臣敢進其說？

translations.literal: At that time too he relied on his lord-father's grace, deeming himself as secure as Mount Tai—how could he know wicked ministers would dare advance their persuasions?
translations.idiomatic: Even then he relied on his father's favor and thought himself as secure as Mount Tai. How could he know that wicked ministers would dare urge him on?

sentences.zh: 向使動靜有常，進退合度，親君子，疏小人，舍浮華，尚恭儉，雖有邪臣間之，何能致慈父之隙？

translations.literal: If only his movements and stillness had constancy, advance and retreat fit measure, drawing near to gentlemen and keeping petty men at a distance, abandoning superficial splendor and honoring respectful frugality—even if wicked ministers came between, how could they bring about a rift with his loving father?
translations.idiomatic: If only his conduct had been steady, his comings and goings proper, if he had drawn near to gentlemen and kept petty men at a distance, abandoned showy luxury and honored modest frugality—even if wicked ministers had sown discord, how could they have estranged him from a loving father?

sentences.zh: 豈不由積德未弘，令聞不著，讒言一至，遂成其禍？

translations.literal: Was it not because accumulated virtue was not broad, good repute not established—when slander arrived once, thus his calamity was made?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not because he had not built up virtue, because his good name was not firmly established, so that when slander came once, disaster followed?

sentences.zh: 竊惟皇儲之寄，荷戴殊重，如其積德不弘，何以嗣守成業？

translations.literal: I privately consider the charge of the imperial heir—the bearing and upholding is especially heavy. If he does not broadly accumulate virtue, how can he inherit and preserve the accomplished enterprise?
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the burden placed on the crown prince is especially heavy. If he does not build up virtue, how can he inherit and preserve an established realm?

sentences.zh: 聖上以殿下親則父子，事兼家國，所應用物，不為節限。

translations.literal: The sage lord, because Your Highness is close as father and son and the affair joins family and state, does not set limits on what may be used.
translations.idiomatic: Because Your Highness is to the sage lord as son to father, and your affairs touch both family and state, no limit is set on what you may use.

sentences.zh: 恩旨未逾六旬，用物已過七萬，驕奢之極，孰雲過此。

translations.literal: The gracious command has not passed sixty days, yet goods used already exceed seventy thousand—arrogance and luxury at the extreme; who would say it surpasses this?
translations.idiomatic: In fewer than sixty days since the gracious edict, your expenditures have already exceeded seventy thousand. For arrogance and luxury, who can say it goes further than this?

sentences.zh: 龍樓之下，惟聚工匠；

translations.literal: Beneath the dragon tower, only craftsmen are gathered;
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the Eastern Palace gather only craftsmen;

sentences.zh: 望苑之內，不睹賢良。

translations.literal: within the vast park, worthy and good men are not seen.
translations.idiomatic: within the pleasure park, no worthy men are to be seen.

sentences.zh: 今言孝敬則闕視膳問安之禮，語恭順則違君父慈訓之方，求風聲則無愛學好道之實，觀舉措則有因緣誅戮之罪。

translations.literal: Now speaking of filial respect, you lack the rites of viewing meals and inquiring after well-being; speaking of respectful obedience, you violate the methods of your lord-father's loving instruction; seeking reputation, there is no reality of loving learning and honoring the Way; observing conduct and movement, there are crimes of killing on pretext.
translations.idiomatic: You speak of filial piety, yet neglect the rites of attending to your father's meals and inquiring after his health. You speak of obedience, yet go against your father's loving instruction. You seek a good reputation, yet show no love of learning or devotion to the Way. As for your conduct, you have been implicated in executions carried out on flimsy grounds.

sentences.zh: 宮臣正士，未嘗在側；

translations.literal: Palace ministers and upright gentlemen have never been at your side;
translations.idiomatic: Upright palace officials are never at your side;

sentences.zh: 群邪淫巧，暱近深宮。

translations.literal: the host of evil, debauched, and crafty draw near within the deep palace.
translations.idiomatic: while a crowd of wicked and crafty men press close within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 愛好者皆游手雜色，施與者併圖畫雕鏤。

translations.literal: Those you love are all idle hands and miscellaneous performers; those you bestow gifts on are altogether painters and carved inlay workers.
translations.idiomatic: Those you favor are idle fellows and low entertainers; those you reward are painters and artisans of carving and inlay.

sentences.zh: 在外瞻仰，已有此失；

translations.literal: To those looking up from outside, these faults already exist;
translations.idiomatic: To those who observe from outside, these faults are already plain;

sentences.zh: 居中隱密，寧可勝計哉！

translations.literal: what lies hidden within—can it be counted!
translations.idiomatic: what goes on in secret within—who can even count it!

sentences.zh: 宣猷禁門，不異阛阓，朝入暮出，穢聲已遠。

translations.literal: The Xuanyou forbidden gate is no different from a market street; entering at dawn and leaving at dusk, foul sounds already carry far.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanyou Gate is no different from a marketplace street. People enter at dawn and leave at dusk, and scandalous rumors already spread far.

sentences.zh: 臣以德音日損，頻上諫書，自爾已來，縱逸尤甚。

translations.literal: Your servant, because virtuous reputation daily declines, has frequently submitted remonstrance memorials; since then, dissipation has been especially extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Because your moral reputation declines daily, I have repeatedly submitted memorials of remonstrance, yet since then your excesses have grown worse still.

sentences.zh: 右庶子趙弘智經明行修，當今善士，臣每奏請，望數召進，與之談論，庶廣徽猷。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Zhao Hongzhi is classic-wise and conduct cultivated, a good man of the present age. Your servant every time memorializes requesting that he be summoned often to enter, to discuss with him, hoping to broaden excellent plans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hongzhi, right vice director, is learned in the classics and upright in conduct—a worthy man of our day. I have repeatedly asked that he be summoned to discuss affairs with you, so that your wisdom might be broadened.

sentences.zh: 令旨反有猜嫌，謂臣妄相推引。

translations.literal: Your command instead has suspicion, saying your servant recklessly recommends and draws in others.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness instead grew suspicious and said I was recklessly pushing my own favorites.

sentences.zh: 從善如流，尚恐不逮；

translations.literal: Following goodness like flowing water—even so one fears not reaching it;
translations.idiomatic: To follow good counsel as readily as flowing water is hard enough to achieve;

sentences.zh: 飾非拒諫，必招敗損。

translations.literal: covering faults and rejecting remonstrance will surely invite defeat and loss.
translations.idiomatic: to cover faults and reject remonstrance is to invite ruin.

sentences.zh: 方崇閉塞之源，不慕欽明之術，雖抱睿哲之資，終罹罔念之咎。

translations.literal: You now exalt the source of obstruction and do not admire the methods of reverent clarity. Though embracing wise and sagely endowment, in the end you will suffer the fault of heedlessness.
translations.idiomatic: You now honor the path of shutting out counsel and do not seek the way of reverent wisdom. Though endowed with keen intelligence, you will in the end suffer for failing to heed good advice.

sentences.zh: 古人云：「苦藥利病，苦言利行。

translations.literal: An ancient said: "Bitter medicine benefits illness; bitter words benefit conduct."
translations.idiomatic: An ancient said, "Bitter medicine cures illness; blunt counsel improves conduct."

sentences.zh: 」伏惟居安思危，日慎一日。

translations.literal: " I bow and consider: dwell in security, think of peril; daily cautious, one day more.
translations.idiomatic: " I humbly beg you to think of danger in times of peace and to grow more cautious day by day.

sentences.zh: 書入，承乾不納，乃遣刺客將加屠害。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Chengqian did not accept it and sent assassins to add slaughter and harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was delivered, Chengqian would not heed it and sent assassins to kill him.

sentences.zh: 俄屬宮廢，玄素隨例除史。

translations.literal: Before long the palace was abolished; Xuansu followed precedent and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when the Eastern Palace was abolished, Xuansu was dismissed from office according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起授潮州刺史，轉鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was restored and appointed governor of Chaozhou, transferred to governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was restored and appointed governor of Chaozhou, then transferred to governor of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: During Yonghui, on account of old age he retired.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era he retired on account of old age.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，加授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longshuo he was additionally granted Silver Glory Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longshuo he was granted the honorary title of Silver Glory Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Linde he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Linde.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：伏伽上疏於高祖，玄素進言於太宗，從疏賤以干至尊，懷切直以明正理，可謂至難矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Fujia submitted memorials to Gaozu; Xuansu advanced words to Taizong. From low and base rank to approach the supreme, harboring urgent straightness to clarify correct principle—this may be called utmost difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Fujia submitted memorials to Gaozu, and Xuansu offered counsel to Taizong. To approach the supreme ruler from humble rank, bearing forthright sincerity to set forth what is right—this may be called the utmost difficulty.

sentences.zh: 既而並見抽獎，咸蒙顧遇。

translations.literal: Afterward both were drawn forth and promoted, all receiving regard and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Both were then promoted and received imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 自非下情忠到，效匪躬之節，上聽聰明，致如流之美，孰能至於此乎？

translations.literal: Unless below loyalty reached its fullness, effecting the integrity of not sparing one's person, and above the hearing was clear and wise, achieving the beauty of following like flowing water—who could reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Had not their loyalty below been complete, had they not given their utmost in service, and had not the rulers above been wise enough to heed remonstrance as flowing water, who could have achieved this?

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Wood that follows the line is made straight; a ruler who follows remonstrance is made sage."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Wood that follows the plumb line is made straight; a ruler who follows remonstrance is made sage."

sentences.zh: 」斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: " This is what it speaks of.
translations.idiomatic: " This is what is meant."

sentences.zh: 世長幼而聰悟，長能規諫；

translations.literal: Shichang was clever and perceptive in youth, and grown could admonish and remonstrate;
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was clever and perceptive from youth and grew able to remonstrate;

sentences.zh: 雲起屏絕朋黨，罔避驕豪。

translations.literal: Yunqi screened off and cut out factional cliques, never avoiding arrogant magnates.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi rejected factional cliques and did not shrink from the proud and powerful.

sentences.zh: 歷覽言行，咸有可觀。

translations.literal: Surveying their words and conduct throughout, all had what could be observed.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing their words and conduct, all had much to admire.

sentences.zh: 而雲起吐茹無方，世長終成詭詐，其不令也宜哉！

translations.literal: Yet Yunqi's spitting and swallowing had no method, and Shichang in the end became deceitful and fraudulent—their lack of excellence is fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yunqi was inconsistent in his dealings, and Shichang in the end proved treacherous. That they did not end well is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 方諸孫、張二子，知不迨矣。

translations.literal: Compared with Sun and Zhang, the two men, in knowledge they do not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Sun Fujia and Zhang Xuansu, they plainly do not measure up.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：言為身文，感義忘身。

translations.literal: The praise says: Words are the pattern of the person; moved by righteousness, one forgets the person.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Words are the ornament of the man; stirred by righteousness, one forgets oneself.

sentences.zh: 不有忠膽，安輕逆鱗？

translations.literal: Without loyal gall, how dare one lightly go against the inverted scales?
translations.idiomatic: Without loyal courage, who would lightly touch the dragon's scales?

sentences.zh: 蘇、韋果俊，伽、素忠純。

translations.literal: Su and Wei were truly outstanding; Fujia and Xuansu were loyal and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Wei were men of real talent; Fujia and Xuansu were loyal and pure.

sentences.zh: 悟主匡失，猗歟諍臣。

translations.literal: Awakening the lord, correcting errors—how admirable, the remonstrating ministers!
translations.idiomatic: They awakened their lords and corrected their faults—how admirable were these remonstrating ministers!
